_comment: THE PRODUCTION-READINESS LEDGER.  This file is the single deterministic
answer to 'is MXFS production ready?' — the `open_defects` criterion FAILS
while any entry below has status != RESOLVED, so showstat can never read
all-green while a credible defect is known-open.
WHY THIS EXISTS (ccloop c7ee71c6 sess21, user directive): the board read
20/20 green through a soft lockup that killed a node for 522 s, an ILOCK
assertion failure on 3 of 4 nodes, and a mkdir(2) that returned success
with the entry existing nowhere.  Behavioural criteria alone cannot carry
this weight: the ones that catch intermittent defects go green whenever a
run gets lucky, and 'this run did not reproduce it' is not 'fixed'.
RULE 6: an entry may move to RESOLVED under exactly two dispositions —
DISPROVED         : direct evidence the reported behaviour was not a defect
FIXED_AND_VERIFIED: RULE 4 proved the cause, the patch targets THAT cause,
and testing which exercises the cause passes cleanly
'Cannot reproduce', 'rare', 'a clean run', 'a plausible explanation', a
workaround, or documentation are NOT dispositions.  Do not delete an entry
to make the board green — that is the one thing this file exists to prevent.

defects.summary: Foreign/adopted journal-slice replay applies BUFFER (and dquot/icreate) image records gated only by upstream XFS_LSN_CMP, but LSNs are incomparable across per-node slices - replay can silently revert survivor-written dir blocks/AG state (false-APPLY) or drop the dead node's fsync-acked changes (false-SKIP)
defects.evidence: Code audit sess32 (session 14): pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1061 (lsn && XFS_LSN_CMP(lsn, current_lsn) >= 0 -> skip) has no foreign gate; xfs_dquot_item_recover.c:145 same; xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:3502 skips the sb-LSN check with a comment stating per-node slice LSNs are not comparable - the same incomparability applies to every buffer record. Inode records ARE correctly gated (di_changecount, node-independent, xfs_inode_item_recover.c:410). The live-replay design comment (xfs_log.c ~712) claims mount-time re-replay is 'LSN-gated and therefore a no-op' - false cross-node. Exposure paths: (1) live foreign replay by the elected survivor; (2) mount-time claim of a dirty slice (slot%%node_count mapping) hours/days after the death, after survivors have rewritten the same blocks; (3) late intent processing by the mount-time claimer against a moved-on filesystem (extent free against possibly-reallocated ranges). GPT sess32 ruling: stop-ship class; containment = skip untagged buf/dquot/icreate images in live foreign replay (inode cc-gate stays); full fix = authority tokens {resource_id, grant_incarnation, tenure_id} captured at logging time + durable held-set manifest + IMAGE_REPLAY_DONE marker gating purge and mount-time image suppression. See ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess32-GPT-ruling-A-D-foreign-replay-stop-ship.
defects.mechanism: Per-node journal slices have independent LSN cycle/block numbering; any cross-slice LSN comparison is meaningless. Buffer replay decides apply-vs-skip by comparing the dead slice's record LSN against the on-disk block LSN stamped by whichever node last flushed that block from ITS slice.
defects.containment: SHIPPED 0.11.273-274, both arms A/B'd on the rig via tests/foreign_replay_ab.sh + rejoin flow: (1) LIVE foreign replay skips untagged buf/dquot/quotaoff/icreate images (P223, knob foreign_replay_untagged_apply=0 default; A/B victims test9/test10: 11-vs-0 skips, both arms full acked visibility 40/40 dirs+files+sizes — records were redundant because the destage kick lands metadata within ~ms of commit). (2) MOUNT-TIME: pass-2 (fresh) disklock claim marks the inherited slice ADOPTED (claim log prints it); xfs_log_mount sets XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE and recovery suppresses untagged images AND the dead incarnation's intents (P226) while inode records keep the cc gate; pass-1 own-stamp reclaim keeps full recovery (own-crash path, grants quarantined). A/B: test11 rejoin default=7 buf images suppressed, mount clean, node sees its full pre-death acked data 40/40/40; test12 rejoin with adopted_slice_full_replay=1 = legacy full replay, no suppression. RESIDUAL (documented, OPEN): held-at-death unlanded records of the skipped types are no longer applied by anyone (bounded durability gap, narrow in practice per the destage-kick timing); adopted-slice intent skip leaks the dead incarnation's incomplete extent-frees (counted via P226; space leak, not corruption). Both residuals close with the full token protocol.

REMAINING FOR THE GATE SWAP: (a) accumulate the would_apply/uncapable_match distribution over more kills and adopted-mount replays — TWO samples so far: sess167 elected arm (capable=1, WOULD_APPLY=7/7, all_apply=2) and sess168 adopted arm on the SAME slice content (capable=0 desc_rc=-2, notheld=7/7, uncap_match=0, WOULD_APPLY=0, txn none=2, csum exact, CAP=1/EVAL=1) — the completed recovery's manifest purge PROVEN observable; keep sampling with every AB kill (harness auto-harvests P273); (b) D-EX-GRANT-EPOCH-NOT-UNIQUE-TENURE-ID must land first — sess166 RULE-5: would_apply is an exploratory UPPER BOUND until the grant-epoch source is per-tenure unique and must not alone justify enforcement; (c) enforcement design per the sess163 hazard list (transaction-atomic rejection, tenure-release invariant, descriptor/DONE crash-resumability).

defects.live_damage_sess41: FIRST LIVE DAMAGE CAPTURE + DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCER (0.11.347, tests/openunlink_deaths.sh unlinker_death, ~2min): B rm's a file A holds open, B killed ~5s later. Foreign replay of B's slice APPLIED the inode item (nlink->0, durable — P92/P19 read disk_nlink=0) but SKIPPED both untagged BUFFER images (P223-FR-UNTAGGED-SKIP type 0x123c n=2,n=3 = the dirent-removal dir block AND the AGI bucket-insert). TRANSACTION ATOMICITY BROKEN by half-application: post-replay state never existed on any node — dirent PRESENT pointing at an nlink=0 inode that is ON NO unlinked bucket (sweep walked nothing; ls shows 'd????????? .oud_1785614151_2571140' on test1 = live namespace corruption; zombie unreachable by any recovery walk = permanent leak + poisoned dirent). NOTE the default foreign_replay_untagged_apply=0 (skip) is itself the damage mechanism here: skipping buffer images while applying the same transaction's inode items is torn recovery. Variance note: an earlier identical run had the AGI insert durable/tagged differently and swept fine — which records get skipped depends on what reached the slice, so both arms (false-skip tear, false-apply revert) are live.

defects.summary: The disklock mount-incarnation identifier (struct mxfs_disklock_ctx.epoch, published as heartbeat record byte offset 24 and carried into every recovery descriptor as victim_epoch/owner_epoch/fence_prover_epoch) is a HARD-CODED ZERO.  Every incarnation-binding predicate in the recovery, fence-certificate and own-slot-CAS paths is therefore vacuous, and step 5.2 of D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES (bind the authority token to the victim incarnation) is unimplementable until it is fixed.
defects.evidence: MEASURED sess83 on the live 32-node CAW rig, independently of the kernel module: raw dd of the 64-slot heartbeat region off the shared LUN (/dev/mapper/mpatha, disklock_offset=67117056 from tools/chk_mxfs -v, 512B records, epoch at byte offset 24), decoded in python3 -> all 31 live records read EPOCH=0; 'distinct EPOCH values across all live HB records: [0]'.  Corroborating: tree-wide grep finds exactly ONE write to ctx->epoch ('ctx->epoch = 0;' dlm/disklock.c:1145); every other occurrence is a read, and hb->epoch = ctx->epoch on every heartbeat/claim write (disklock.c:647, :2037, :4110, :4248).
defects.mechanism: Vacuous predicates, all dlm/disklock.c: (1) hb_own_record() :457 tests cur->epoch == ctx->epoch = 0==0, so a stale ACTIVE record left by our OWN previous incarnation reads as our live record and hb_foreign_kind()'s 'a different incarnation of this node owns the slot' branch :482 is unreachable; (2) desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch :2483 :3121 = 0, so the durable recovery descriptor cannot name which incarnation of the victim it is recovering; (3) d->owner_epoch == ctx->epoch (:1604 :1702 :2380 :2437 :2892 :3080 :3368 :3511) collapses to owner_node == local_node, so a REJOINED incarnation of the same node adopts its own prior incarnation's recovery lease; (4) same for d->fence_prover_epoch == ctx->epoch (:2895 :3257) in the sess75/76 fence certificate; (5) the guard idiom 'if (victim_epoch && d->victim_epoch != victim_epoch) refuse' (:2462 :2954 :3069 :3489 ...) is SKIPPED at ~8 recovery sites (recovery_begin, takeover, fence_intent, fence_certify, claim, advance) because callers pass an epoch read from disk, i.e. 0; (6) mxfs_disklock_slot_holds_incarnation() degenerate; (7) :290 'return epoch == 0 || d->victim_epoch == epoch;' always true.
defects.containment: None.  The defect is silent: it weakens checks that already appear to pass.  No workaround exists and none is acceptable (RULE 6).
defects.next: CLOSED sess91.  Residual follow-up tracked on D-RECOV-ADVANCE-UNBOUNDED-RETRY: inject a same-node later incarnation attempting to advance a predecessor's descriptor and assert the owner-epoch predicate refuses it.
defects.found: sess83
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess91.  CAUSE (RULE 4): tree-wide grep found exactly one write to the identifier, 'ctx->epoch = 0' (dlm/disklock.c:1145), and a raw O_DIRECT decode of the 64-slot heartbeat region on the live LUN read EPOCH=0 on all 31 live records (sess83).  PATCH: 0.11.420 gives every mount a random nonzero 64-bit incarnation per the sess83 RULE-5 ruling and threads it through the heartbeat, death, descriptor and fence-certificate paths.  VERIFICATION that exercises the cause, all on the live 32-node CAW rig: (a) sess88 — 32/32 on-disk incarnations nonzero, 32/32 distinct, bit lengths 58-64; the same measurement that returned '[0]' at sess83. (b) sess88 — a hard kill made all 31 survivors log P163-RECOVERY-PENDING naming the victim by its EXACT pre-kill on-disk incarnation, and P234-RECOV-FENCED carried that incarnation into the durable descriptor (ledger mechanism item 2). (c) sess88 — the incarnation CHANGES across a remount of the same host, which is what makes it an incarnation rather than a node id. (d) sess91 — the decisive step, because (a)-(c) only prove the identifier is nonzero, not that the COMPARISONS became live.  tests/incarnation_mismatch_probe.sh reaches the refusal arms through the monitor's epoch-change path (disklock.c:1147) by rewriting only the 8-byte epoch field of a dead node's sector, with the feature CRC recomputed so the record stays valid.  ALL THREE arms that sess88 and sess89 recorded as never having executed on the rig fired, and each took the correct branch: arm=zero gave 'P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH slot=4 victim=4085327405 victim_inc=1634619062121349274 slot_inc=0 ... refusing to publish' plus P234-COMPLETE-FENCEFAIL rc=-116 and NO descriptor published (mechanism items 5 and 7 — zero is not a wildcard); arm=nonzero gave 'P237-RECOV-SUPERSEDED slot=29 victim_inc=383883444245855066 slot_inc=15952125467273129900 — retiring our pending recovery instead of guarding a LIVE member' plus P237-COMPLETE-SUPERSEDED, with no guard laid; and the follow-on round exercised P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED through to P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE + P97-SWEEP-DONE.  The owner-incarnation predicates (mechanism items 3 and 4) are exercised POSITIVELY by every one of those completions: recov_auth_holds and recov_fence_auth_holds both require inc_eq(d->owner_epoch, ctx->epoch) and inc_eq(d->fence_prover_epoch, ctx->epoch) to hold on real nonzero values before a descriptor may be certified or advanced. (e) Regression gate: full 32/caw board GREEN on 0.11.420 (sess90) and again on 0.11.421 (sess91) — 27 of 27 functional criteria PASS, open_defects red by policy only. NOT CLAIMED, and carried forward as an explicit item on D-RECOV-AUTH-ZERO-VICTIM-EPOCH-WEDGE's successor entries: the NEGATIVE arm of the owner/prover-incarnation tests (a same-node LATER incarnation attempting to advance or certify a predecessor's descriptor — the 'A -> B -> A within a single session' case in disklock.h:261) was not injected.  Every arm that was injected refused or branched correctly, and no arm published against an incarnation the slot did not carry.

defects.summary: mkdir(2) returns success while the directory entry exists on no node
defects.evidence: TWO independent byte-exact captures, ccloop c7ee71c6 sess22: sfstorm_20260729_003736 r32 ino=44040321 test31 node31_1; sfstorm_20260729_005540 r39 ino=56623307 test27 node27_1. Both nlink=33 visible=31 expected=32 identical on ALL 32 nodes, zero nonzero mkdir(2) rc cluster-wide.
defects.mechanism: P65-EPOCH-CONVGATE requests reload+adopt (peer converted the dir). P34J-RELOAD-DEMOTE-BAIL abandons that reload whenever a release drain is concurrently active -- its own comment promises 'the caller retries once the demote completes', which NO caller implemented. i_dlm_dir_valid_epoch therefore stays behind the master dir_epoch, and P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE then skips EVERY flush of whatever the operation goes on to commit (observed firing 3x for one inode: from mkdir, xfsaild and a kworker). The drain exits flushed=1 with pending!=durable (P196 cls=UNCOPIED: never copied into any outgoing image), hands off the grant (P188), and the next adopt discards the change (P177).
defects.detector: P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE count tracks durable losses almost 1:1 (p32e=6/7/9 -> 3/4/4 losses). P195 is the state-reached precursor; dirent_durability the intermittent symptom.
defects.blocking_fix: Adopt at EX ACQUIRE, before the tenure is exposed to the operation, so P195 never fires at all. The sess22 fix (reload_demote_wait_ms) makes the adopt HAPPEN rather than never, but it still happens after the op gate has noticed -- P195 still fires 5-7x per POST run, i.e. a tenure still mutates an epoch-stale base and then recovers.
attempted_and_refuted: P193 epoch-override at the conversion gate — A/B measured A=0 B=0 failing rounds, no effect; the review showed it is at the wrong layer
dir_lookup_freshness_gate — measured to NEVER engage: dirty_here=1 in 100% of genuine forward-stale hits, so the tenure has always already mutated by the lookup
create_baseline_trackers — A/B was counter-directional (P195: 0 with fix off, 1 with fix on, n=1 per arm); principled and retained, but NOT validated

P197-P6-PREMISE (sess22) REFUTED the tenure-identity hypothesis: i_mxfs_ex_grant_seq IS correctly re-stamped. premise=ok in 60/60 and in both loss captures (dirty_age_ms=6, tenure_age_ms=6). Do not re-chase 'the tenure stamp was carried over'.

tests/creator_stale_base.sh (sess22): a designated-creator + quiet-window harness. Constructs the epoch-stale precondition en masse (3000+ P65 per run) but the adopt always succeeds and it NEVER loses an entry. The loss needs the CONCURRENT release drain that only the full 32-way race produces. Reproducing needs sf_mkdir_storm.sh at 60 rounds -- 30 is not enough on current builds; both captures were round >30.

progress_sess22.fix: v0.11.174 mxfs.reload_demote_wait_ms=50 -- mxfs_dlm_reload_inode now WAITS (bounded, 1ms steps) for an active release drain instead of abandoning the reload, implementing the contract P34J's comment already stated. Bounded so a drain blocked on a lock we hold costs only the bound, never a deadlock.

progress_sess22.PRE_all_fixes_off: durable rounds 3, 4, 4, 1 (n=4, every one the single-name shape nlink=33 visible=31) | p32e 6,7,9,3 | p34jbail 936,874,641
progress_sess22.POST_all_fixes_on: durable rounds 0 x 7 fresh-prep runs, zero of ANY shape | p32e 0 | p34jbail 0 | p198waited 617,567,497,...
progress_sess22.cost: P198 wait: mean 4.06 ms, 254 of 567 waited 1 ms, 2.3 s total cluster-wide across a 120 s storm. No RULE 0 concern.
progress_sess22.why_still_open: RULE 6 needs the DEFECT resolved, not just the observed symptom suppressed. P195 (mutation on an epoch-stale base) still fires 5-7x per POST run, so the invariant is still violated and the state is still reachable; recovery-after-the-fact is not the same as prevention.

defects.NEW_SYMPTOM_SHAPE_sess25: A dirent_durability FAIL observed this session has a DIFFERENT shape from the captured single-name loss and should not be assumed to be the same defect. test22 reported r21 and r22 each missing 28 of 32 peers (everyone except node1/node2/node16/node22), for a CONTIGUOUS TAIL of rounds (8 of the 10 judged rounds, 21-28), while the other 31 nodes all reported durable_loss=0. 28 simultaneous losses agreed by nobody else is not 28 lost mkdirs -- it is ONE node's directory view going stale at a point in time and never converging. Contrast the captured D-SILENT-MKDIR-LOSS shape: nlink=33 visible=31 expected=32, i.e. exactly ONE name, agreed by ALL nodes. Also: on the reporting node P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE, P195, P188 and P34J all read ZERO, so none of this defect's own detectors fired. Treat as a candidate SEPARATE read-side staleness defect until evidence ties them together.
defects.progress_sess26: MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED; defect stays OPEN because the causal link to the observed losses is correlational, not a byte-exact chain. Method: every documented chain marker (P32E/P195/P188/P177/P146V/P51/P65/P194) read ZERO in a losing window (all 11 probes first confirmed present via strings mxfs.ko), so the producer had no probe. tests/dd_loss_differential.sh differenced per-token probe frequencies between the losing node and its 31 peers in one scoped window and nominated P6-MIDTENURE-RELOAD-SKIP: loser 661 vs peer median 37 (range 25-215), 3x above the highest peer, nothing else comparable. MECHANISM: that branch clears i_dlm_stale and returns WITHOUT reloading, premise 'dirtied under the current EX tenure so the platter has nothing to teach us'. P197 shows the premise is literally true; the INFERENCE is false when a peer published since. New P81-P6-SRC histogram shows the swallowed staleness comes from srcs 2/5/7/8, ALL peer-driven (2 = consuming a peer's DIR_MODIFY; 5 = set at release, a peer may have held EX throughout; 7 = the else-branch of dir_slow_skip, i.e. a peer handoff DID occur; 8 = MXFS_IF_DIR_RELOAD consumed on the EX-acquire fast path). At src=8 the flag is CLEARED before the reload is attempted, so skipping destroys the notification on both channels and the peer's entry is never observed. New per-inode i_dlm_p6skip_n shows this repeats: repeat_max 20-29 consecutive skips with no real reload. mxfs.p6_epoch_override could never help -- it honours only src==3, and losing windows show epoch == entry_epoch throughout. FIX: mxfs.p6_honor_src_mask (default 0x1A4 = srcs 2,5,7,8) in pal/linux/xfs_aops.c; the skip does not apply to staleness from those sources. 0 = pre-fix, same-build A/B. RULE 0 CONSTRAINT: the obvious fix (p6_midtenure_skip=0, always reload) takes dirent_durability from 120s to a 240s/240s TIMEOUT and is forbidden; the mask reloads only on peer notifications and costs nothing. PAIRED MEASUREMENT, one build (0.11.228, 8E827AAB556A0E21AF739C9), knob flipped at runtime -- swallowed notifications (hist 2+5+7+8) test1/test5/test19: 173/43/42 at mask=0 vs 0/0/0 at 0x1A4; repeat_ge8 86/36/44 -> 0/0/0; repeat_max 29/20/24 -> 0/0/0. dirent_durability PASS 124s, cache_coherency 654/654 26s, dir_reuse_coherency 65/65 102s. WHY STILL OPEN: observed loss rate is ~2 in 12 runs, so the 4 post-fix passes and 3 pre-fix passes accumulated so far cannot distinguish the arms on the LOSS itself. The swallowed-notification count is a far more sensitive proxy (~42/node/run -> 0) and it is eliminated, but RULE 6 defines this defect by the loss. Next: alternate p6_honor_src_mask 0x1A4/0 across many paired runs and compare durable_loss rates; also consider whether src=1 (readdir refresh, the largest bucket, no repeat streaks) needs honouring (mask 0x1A6).
defects.loss_rate_tally_sess26: RUN TALLY, one build (v0.11.223-0.11.228, p6_honor_src_mask flipped at runtime). Counting only GENUINE single-node durable losses (normal ~120s wall, late_ok>0, states:FAIL=1) and excluding rank1 240s truncations, which are a separate pace failure (see D-MOUNT-DEGRADES-WITH-USE) and occurred in BOTH arms: PRE-FIX (mask=0 or pre-fix builds): 2 genuine losses in ~12 runs -- test19 durable_loss=8 late_ok=4 at 119s, and test4 durable_loss=8 late_ok=14 at 120s. POST-FIX (mask=0x1A4): 0 genuine losses in ~16 runs. If the pre-fix rate (~0.17) were unchanged, 0 in 16 has probability ~0.05, so this is suggestive but at the edge of significance -- NOT a disposition on its own. The strong evidence remains the mechanism metric: swallowed peer notifications ~42/node/run -> 0, and consecutive-skip streaks (i_dlm_p6skip_n) max 29 -> 0. The rank1 240s truncations (3 observed: durable_loss 8/8/5, late_ok 0/10/14) are NOT this defect -- P6-MIDTENURE-RELOAD-SKIP is absent from their differentials and they occur pre- and post-fix alike.
defects.sess27_create_baseline_is_DEAD_CODE: PROVEN: mxfs.create_baseline_trackers (sess21) has NEVER EXECUTED ONCE. The block lives in mxfs_dlm_grant_local_new (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~27477) and is gated on S_ISDIR(VFS_I(ip)->i_mode), but its only caller is xfs_iget_cache_miss under XFS_IGET_CREATE (xfs_icache.c:1885) where the inode was just allocated and i_mode is still 0 -- the mode is set later by xfs_init_new_inode, and even the generation is only assigned at xfs_icache.c:1902. New probe P209-CREATE-BASELINE, placed INSIDE the block, read ZERO on every node across a full 32-node dirent_durability run. This explains the ledger note that sess21's paired A/B was 'counter-directional and never validated': the knob is a no-op, so both arms were the same code. DO NOT treat create_baseline_trackers as a live lever. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT in the same block: even if reached, it does `if (bgg) ... if (bep) ...` on values read from the DLM for a brand-new inode created WITHOUT a real acquire (deferred publish), so the DLM has no grant record and both read 0 -- the guards would skip and the sentinels would survive anyway. Fixing the S_ISDIR gate alone is therefore NOT sufficient; the stamp has to happen where the grant actually becomes real (the deferred publish), or the 'never set' sentinel 0 has to be replaced by a distinct 'self-created, coherent as of creation' value so the detectors gated on cached_grant_gen != 0 stop being inert for self-created directories.
defects.sess27_detector_restored: dirent_publish_integrity is a WORKING detector again (it had been scanning zero kernel lines -- see the sess27 evidence-integrity note). Live capture, test8, in-window: P194-EPOCH-STALE-OP ino=4194443 op=lookup grant_epoch=2 valid_epoch=0 dlm_mode=5 fmt=1 size=6 dirty_here=1 name=node8 comm=mkdir, then P195-STALE-BASE-ALREADY-DIRTY grant_gen=3098 cached_gen=0 gen_moved=1 dirty_seq=474 ex_grant_seq=474. By the probe's OWN documented discriminator gen_moved=1 means the lock changed hands while i_mxfs_ex_grant_seq failed to reflect it -- the tenure-tracking root, not the epoch source. And cached_gen=0 is the never-set sentinel, i.e. the creator case above.

defects.sess27_EIGHT_NODE_CAPTURE_racebail_1to1: STRONGEST LEAD IN SEVERAL SESSIONS. Caught during the D-MATRIX-UNMEASURED sweep at 8/caw on 0.11.237: dirent_durability FAIL nodes_pass=7/8, test3 'rounds=30 durable_loss=5 late_ok=15 mkdir_err=0' at a 91s wall (well inside the 240s budget), so by the recorded discriminator (late_ok>0 at a normal wall) this is a GENUINE failure, not a straggler-timeout artifact. defects.sess28_ROOT_PROVEN_cross_incarnation_epo: ROOT PROVEN BY TRACE AND FIXED (RULE 4 step 2b), build 0.11.242 C6D909C4133BA6731C55251. THE DEFECT: the CAW dir_epoch is a property of the inode NUMBER, not of an incarnation. caw_tombstone_slot() and caw_claim_inherit_epoch() (dlm/dlm_caw.c ~897/920) deliberately carry dir_epoch across an idle gap, and mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_dir_epoch() serves it out of a per-resource grant_meta cache that survives the inode being freed and re-created. So every consumer's `master_epoch > i_dlm_dir_valid_epoch` test compares a DEAD incarnation's handoff lineage against a LIVE incarnation's baseline -- the same invalid cross-incarnation comparison class sess27 proved for di_gen in RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP. TRACE (2/caw test2, one inode's full scoped window, ino 2099630): line 119 'P9-NLEDGE reset4create' = incarnation A created; line 126 'P210-CREATOR-BASELINE site=2 bep=0' = A published at epoch 0; A then handed off (P70-BP EXIT=full / P-DIRBAST) driving the SLOT epoch to 2; line 1363 'EVICT-RING-FLAG incore_gen=2916713347 freed_gen=2916713348' = A FREED; line 1383 'reset4create' = incarnation B created on the same number; line 1410 'P195-STALE-BASE-ALREADY-DIRTY grant_epoch=2 valid_epoch=0 self_created=1 baseline_unset=1 comm=mkdir'. B is brand new, created by this node, and at that moment still i_dlm_unpublished -- it has NO DLM grant of its own -- yet reads grant_epoch=2 out of A's stale grant_meta. CONSEQUENCE: the comparison is permanently true for B, so P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE (mxfs.dir_epoch_flush_fence, ships 1) skips flushes of B's directory. Note the shipped asymmetry this exposes: the CONSUMER of the baseline ships ENABLED while the only maintainer that would advance it on a handoff (mxfs.dir_epoch_adopt) ships DISABLED, because sess49 proved enabling it causes an AG double-free and FS shutdown. THE FIX: mxfs.dir_epoch_incarn_gate (NEW, ships 1) -- new field i_dlm_dir_valid_incarn records the i_generation the baseline was established under, stamped at all 11 assignment sites; new predicate mxfs_dir_epoch_superseded() replaces the raw compare in BOTH consumers (P32E in xfs_inode.c, the P194/P195 gate in libxfs/xfs_dir2.c). defects.mechanism: No closed submission gate + drain-to-zero before handoff. Includes: a partial inode-cluster write whose buffer completion marks EVERY attached inode durable, including ones whose sectors were dropped; and no per-tenure in-flight write accounting, so a write submitted while ownership was valid can land after a later tenure's.
defects.detector: P188-REL-OBLIGATION-AT-UNLOCK plus P196-UNLOCK-OBLIGATION-CLASS (sess22), which names WHICH of four causes each occurrence is: NODRAIN / REDIRTY / INFLIGHT / UNCOPIED.
defects.blocking_fix: Close the tenure to new submissions, commit, publish, wait for every write attributed to the tenure, account completion only for bytes actually issued, verify pending==durable, THEN bump the published epoch and release. Infrastructure already half-exists: b_tenure_id (per-buffer tenure attribution) and i_mxfs_ex_grant_seq (live per-tenure counter for dirs, measured egseq!=0 in 7122/7122 P68-EVDECIDE).
attempted_and_refuted: pub_skip_rearm (re-arm the skipped inode as still-dirty) — MEASURED LIVELOCK: the skip happens precisely because publication authority is absent, so the retry can never succeed. The retry must happen BEFORE release, while the grant is still held.

progress_sess22.classified: Every P196 observed reads cls=UNCOPIED with drain_ran=1 drain_flushed=1 (e.g. dr_pend=17 dr_dur=12 dr_flush=12). NOT a timing race (INFLIGHT) and NOT a post-drain re-dirty (REDIRTY): the drain returned success on an inode whose committed change was never staged into any outgoing image.
progress_sess22.consequence_for_the_fix: Enforcing at the drain (mxfs.pub_obligation_enforce) CANNOT close this: the retry re-runs a flush that is fenced further down by P32E. That is the real reason sess20's re-arm livelocked, and it retires 'add a drain-to-zero wait' as the fix shape for this site.

gpt_detector_design_sess29.priority: GPT ranks this the highest-leverage remaining defect: it can invalidate the authority premise of the sess29 cluster fix, explain dirent_publish_integrity's unlanded_at_unlock=1, plausibly cause the silent mkdir loss, and contaminate several coherency/pace observations.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.do_not_infer_home_visibility_from: transaction commit; log force completion; AIL insertion; I/O submission; buffer dirty state transiently clearing. A log force makes a change durable in the JOURNAL, not visible at its HOME block, and peers do not replay another mounted node's log.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.cheapest_strong_primitive: an exact home-I/O COMPLETION CERTIFICATE attached to the change when it is made -- i.e. hook the real buffer/log-item iodone, not any earlier stage.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.scope_warning: the association must cover ALL peer-visible blocks, not just the inode core. For mkdir that includes parent dir DATA, parent inode, child inode, and the dir/free-space metadata lookup depends on. An inode-level release certificate is insufficient when the visible state lives in a directory data block.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.use_dlm_epochs_not_wall_clock: the sess29 cross-node merge technique is reusable but should key on causal identifiers -- DLM resource, authority epoch/grant sequence, local dirty generation, release sequence, home submission+completion sequence, next grant sequence -- rather than CLOCK_REALTIME.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.optional_strong_validation: sampled peer-side home read: before release, digest the authoritative home image and publish identity/generation/digest (an LVB is a natural carrier); on the next grant, invalidate the receiver's cached copy and read home directly, comparing incarnation/generation/CRC/digest. Diagnostic arm only. A buffered read may just return another stale cache image -- it must be a real post-invalidation read.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.the_barrier_itself: 1 stop new modifications under the current authority epoch; 2 identify every home obligation from that epoch; 3 journal ordering/durability; 4 push those exact items to home; 5 WAIT for real successful home-I/O completion; 6 publish the completed release generation; 7 end authority / permit the peer grant. A plain log force is only step 3. Keep the DLM grant blocked until completion -- do not release first and finish asynchronously. If lock ordering forbids waiting inside mxfs_dlm_ilock_end, use a prepare-release phase or workqueue state machine.

sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.what_the_ledger_asked_for: The standing complaint on this defect is that the pending-vs-durable predicate is evaluated on ONE early-exit branch (P176) and NEVER at the wire unlock. BUILT sess30.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.predicate: XFS's own per-inode flush flag. XFS_IFLUSHING (1<<7 in ip->i_flags) is set by xfs_iflush when it copies the in-core image into a cluster buffer and cleared only by that buffer's iodone. So `IFLUSHING at unlock` means verbatim: we are handing the tenure away while bytes produced under it are staged in a buffer that has not reached home.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.sites: mxfs_dlm_relbar_check() at BOTH bast_process release tails (arm=noanchor, arm=anchored), immediately before the wire unlock; PLUS mxfs_relbar_epoch_check() at ALL NINE i_dlm_epoch bump sites (every site that ENDS a tenure: bast_process x3, bast_notify, ilock_begin x2, evict x2, peer_joined_flush). Read with `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/release_barrier_dump` -> P220-RELEASE-BARRIER-TOTAL unlocks/flushing/in_ail/pinned/epoch_ends/epoch_flushing. Probes P220-UNLOCK-OBLIGATION-OPEN and P220-EPOCH-OBLIGATION-OPEN (the latter carries epsrc = __LINE__ of the bump site, so the leaking path is NAMED).
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.lockless_by_design: mxfs_relbar_epoch_check reads ip->i_flags directly rather than via xfs_iflags_test(), because several bump sites hold ip->i_dlm_lock and xfs_iflags_test takes ip->i_flags_lock -- nesting a second inode spinlock inside the DLM lock for a diagnostic is not worth the lock-order risk.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.first_readings: unlocks=9975/5224/9740 flushing=0 in_ail=0 pinned=0; epoch_ends=11204 epoch_flushing=0. SOLID NEGATIVE for the two bast_process tails: the existing release drain leaves nothing staged there.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.IMPORTANT_do_not_over_read: Those readings came from runs in which P219 stale_tenure was ALSO 0 -- i.e. the runs never exercised the condition (host contention truncated them). The hypothesis 'the tenure ends while a staged image is outstanding' is therefore UNTESTED, not refuted. It needs ONE clean run with a full workload and both detectors armed.

gpt_barrier_design_sess30.invariant: No write containing bytes produced under grant tenure A may remain queued or in flight when tenure A is handed to another node. Stronger than 'check authority at copy-in' and stronger than 'wait for the flush lock'.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.iflock_is_only_a_proxy: It can be cleared by abort/error/shutdown without successful home publication; checking it ONCE is racy (clear -> local op stages -> unlock); it says nothing about dirty state that has not reached xfs_iflush yet. Prefer an explicit per-tenure outstanding-publication COUNT.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.sequence: 1 BAST marks REVOKING and CLOSES ADMISSION (do not block in the AST); 2 drain active users; 3 force log to unpin; 4 flush dirty-but-not-staged while EX is still retained; 5 arrange submission of already-staged buffers; 6 WAIT for successful completion holding NO ILOCK / flush lock / buffer lock / AIL lock / transaction or AG lock / DLM internal lock; 7 recheck a generation counter for work that appeared during the drain; 8 only then downgrade/unlock.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.admission_race: 'Wait if iflock held, else release' is NOT sufficient -- admission must be closed BEFORE examining state, or: worker sees iflock clear -> local op stages and takes iflock -> worker unlocks -> staged write lands later.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.delwri_hazard: Do NOT steal or independently submit a buffer from a delwri list xfsaild currently owns: the buffer lock does not confer ownership of b_list. Correct shape is an ownership-aware rendezvous -- release worker sets an urgent-submit bit, the current list owner submits normally, iodone wakes the waiter.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.clustering_warning: Avoid broad xfs_iflush_cluster from the release path: it stages neighbouring slots whose DLM authority and release state differ. In MXFS clustering is no longer merely a performance choice, it creates cross-authority coupling.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.failure_policy: If the home write FAILS, 'unlock anyway' recreates the corruption window. Either retain the grant and retry, or fence. A timed-out write is especially dangerous: timed out does not mean it cannot complete later.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.submit_time_check_role: Keep the submit-time epoch check as a PERMANENT INVARIANT ASSERTION / fail-stop, not as the recovery mechanism. Correct re-arming at submit time is far more invasive (undo flush state for every attached item, keep each in the AIL, restore watermarks, prevent buffer-wide iodone retiring them, distinguish retryable state from a peer-freed inode) and 'retry after reacquiring EX' is not universally valid -- reacquiring EX does not make an obsolete incarnation current again.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.scope_warning: An inode-only barrier will NOT cover the authority domain. The same copy-in/submit-across-release window exists for directory and attribute blocks, bmap btree blocks, remote attr blocks, and (on the AG/global resources) AGI/AGF/AGFL, inode and free-space btrees, rmap/refcount, quota. Suggested general detector: per-buffer provenance (owning lock domain + resource tenure/epoch at last authoritative modification), and for inode clusters it must stay PER SLOT because one physical buffer spans multiple authority domains.

defects.summary: A workload that meets its budget on a fresh prep cannot finish after the same mount has been used
defects.evidence: 32/caw@0.11.163 rsync_paired: PASS 14s fresh vs 0/32 hung at 60s after prior work. 32/caw@0.11.163 crash_consistency: 32/32 fresh vs 31/32. 32/caw@0.11.167 crash_consistency: PASS 57s fresh vs 0/32 hung at 90s. The IDENTICAL 13-test sequence on a fresh prep passes every time, so it is accumulated mount state, not test ordering.
defects.mechanism: TWO components rooted. (1) sess28: xfs_dir2_readdir.c retried a reload 200x with msleep(1) while the caller held ILOCK_SHARED, so every round bailed -- 1210ms -> 5ms per getdents (242x). (2) sess29 ROOT PROVEN + FIXED: the demoter claim taken by mxfs_inode_dlm_defer_bast is deliberately RETAINED by mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks' P152 punt (the only exit in the tree that skips its clear) so the committing task stays exempt across its post-commit xfs_iunlock -- and NOTHING ever ended that retention. The dwork that inherits the release lands in slot 2 and clears slot 2 only. mxfs_foreign_demoter() then stays true for the life of the in-core inode, so EVERY reload pays mxfs.reload_demote_wait_ms and abandons with i_dlm_stale set (224-354 bails on ONE inode vs 1 on healthy nodes). Second propagation step: the inode is freed still claimed, alloc_inode_sb does not zero the slab object, and the initializer's MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER refuses a non-owner clear -- so the NEXT inode on that memory is born stranded carrying a dead task's stamps. Decisive counter: P215-DEFER set=2 clear=0 retain=2 on four nodes, i.e. every deferral punted and the inline clear never ran.
defects.detector: Per-phase timers in tests/suite/sustained_load.sh (setup/rmrf/mkb/syn/bar1/mkd/bar2): compare rmrf on a fresh prep against the same mount after a full board. The aggregate per_op hides it -- sess28 measured ~97% of the criterion's wall outside the only thing it was timing. For the demoter component use tests/demoter_strand_census.sh.
defects.blocking_fix: unknown — suspects: DLM lock-table growth, AG grant-cache churn, inode cache/AIL growth, CAW slot-table pressure, per-AG counters that never reset

defects.REPRODUCED_sess25:
REPRODUCED ON THE CURRENT BUILD with a clean paired measurement, and the trigger is now NARROWED. Same build 0.11.210, same 32-node cluster, same criteria:
  fresh prep            : cache_coherency PASS 35s/60s   dlm_fairness PASS 26s/30s
  2nd run, same prep    : cache_coherency PASS 31s/60s
  after ONE dirent_durability storm on that mount:
                          cache_coherency FAIL 60s/60s NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32
                          dlm_fairness    FAIL 30s/30s NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32
                          zero_silent_loss PASS but 50s vs 28s fresh
So it is NOT cumulative age and NOT 'any prior work' -- a second run on the same mount is still fast. It is a HEAVY STORM specifically. That also explains why sustained_load was refuted as the detector in sess22 (14 consecutive runs, no progressive decline): sustained_load is not a storm. IMPORTANT for future sessions: this confounds any regression test run on an aged mount. Two criteria were briefly suspected of being a regression from this session's demoter change and were exonerated by re-running on a fresh prep; P73-WAITSTALL was 0 throughout, so the slowdown is NOT demote-wait stalls.
defects.NARROWING_sess25:
tests/mount_degrade_probe.sh (new) times three primitives per node with NO barrier, so the per-node DISTRIBUTION is visible -- which the criteria cannot show, because one straggler holding a barrier reports as NO_TERMINAL_RECORD on ALL ranks and is indistinguishable from every node being slow. Paired FRESH vs POST_STORM, 32 nodes, same build 0.11.210:
  metric            FRESH(min/med/max)         POST_STORM(min/med/max)
  statfs            58.9 / 70.9 / 84.4 ms      58.4 / 73.1 / 96.4 ms
  shared-dir mkdir  18876 / 28208 / 29866 ms   481 / 26983 / 28901 ms
  private mkdir     846 / 2634 / 3957 ms       411 / 642 / 31752 ms
  private max/min   4.7x                       77.3x
THREE SOLID CONCLUSIONS:
  1. statfs is UNCHANGED (71 vs 73 ms median, 1.4-1.7x spread in both). The filesystem service      path does not degrade at all.
  2. Shared-directory mkdir costs the SAME fresh and post-storm (28208 vs 26983 ms median for 20      mkdir+rmdir = ~1.4 s/op). So the storm does NOT degrade shared-dir throughput; that ~1.4 s/op      is D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE and is storm-INDEPENDENT.
  3. The post-storm signature is a SINGLE-NODE OUTLIER, not a uniform shift: private max/min goes      4.7x -> 77.3x, driven by one node (test25) at 31752 ms against a 642 ms median. That node was      NOT wedged -- load 0.45, no D-state, no P73-WAITSTALL -- but showed P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=137      isdir=1 req_mode=5 dur_ms=1056..2396, i.e. multi-second EX acquires on the shared directory.
REFRAME: 'the mount degrades' is probably the wrong model. The evidence says ONE NODE BECOMES A PERSISTENT STRAGGLER after a storm (slow, not stuck), and because every barrier criterion needs all N ranks, that one node fails the whole board. Same blast-radius shape as the two wedges fixed this session, but a slowdown rather than a deadlock.
PROBE LIMITATION, stated so the numbers are not over-read: the three phases are NOT synchronised across nodes, so a node lagging in its private phase overlaps its peers' shared phase. That makes the private MEDIANS non-comparable between runs (FRESH's 2634 ms median is higher than POST_STORM's 642 ms purely because all 32 nodes ran private simultaneously on the fresh run). The SPREAD and the statfs/shared columns are sound; the private median is not. Next session: add a coord barrier between phases, then re-run the pair.

defects.localised_sess26: CORRECTION OF AN EARLIER SESS26 CLAIM. Two independent 240s/240s dirent_durability truncations on an aged mount, BOTH on test1 (= rank 1), never any other node -- that part holds. The token differential vs the 31 peers showed test1 elevated on P1-AGWAIT (x25-28), P128-INACT-DEFER (x154-177), P-DIRFLUSH (x18-24) and doing none of the peers' eviction work, and I initially recorded those probes as naming the backlog. THEY DO NOT. Measured afterwards on a FRESH-PREP PASSING run (117s, 32/32, durable_loss=0) with tests/rank1_straggler_probe.sh: rank1 is ALREADY above every peer on exactly those probes, at the same magnitudes -- P128-INACT-DEFER 157 (peer max 2) vs 153-176 when failing; P-DIRFLUSH 800 (peer max 56) vs 615-773 when failing; P1-AGWAIT 92 (peer max 6) vs 110-200; P-BLOCK0-CONVGATE 62 (peers 0); P-IGET-ENOENT 40 (peers 0); EVICT-RING-FLAG 0 vs median 23. So the elevation is the COORDINATOR ROLE, present on healthy passing runs, and it does not discriminate failing from passing. METHOD LESSON: a loser-vs-peers differential is only valid when the losing node is an ordinary peer. If the loser is rank 1, the role asymmetry alone yields x20-x158 departures and swamps any real signal -- compare rank1-failing against rank1-PASSING instead. (The P6-MIDTENURE finding for D-SILENT-MKDIR-LOSS is unaffected: that loser was test4, an ordinary peer, and P6 sits at x1.6 on rank1 so the role does not explain it.) WHAT REMAINS ESTABLISHED: the 240s truncations happen only on an aged mount and only on rank1; a fresh prep on the same build/mask passes at 116-124s (11 runs). The CAUSE is not yet named. SECOND METHOD CORRECTION: 'diff rank1-failing against rank1-passing' is ALSO invalid as naively executed. Probe pr_warn counters are static atomic_t = PER MODULE LOAD and capped, so they never reset between runs on one mount. Diffing a late (failing) run against a fresh-prep (passing) run measures CAP EXHAUSTION: measured top rows were P170-CLWR 800->0 (its documented cap is exactly 800, see pal/linux/xfs_buf.c ~3747), P25-INSTR 600->0, P141-UNLK-EXCLR 500->0, P82-ADD/P19-B3DEC/P140-RECLAIM-COMMIT 300->0 -- round numbers to zero, entirely artifact. VALID DESIGN: match the ORDINAL run position after a fresh prep. The mount fails at iteration k; prep again, run k iterations (expected to pass at k), and diff the two iteration-k censuses -- same node, same role, same module age. Or get the failure to occur on the FIRST run after a prep, making any fresh-prep run a like-for-like control. REPRODUCTION RATE for that design: fresh prep then 1-2 passes at 116-124s, then a 240s rank1 truncation; observed 3 times (durable_loss=8, 8, 5; late_ok 10, 14, and one 0). See ccmemory probe-counts-are-per-module-load-and-capped.
defects.sess28_QUANTIFIED_DOSE_RESPONSE: sustained_load IS a detector at 32 nodes on the current build, contradicting sess22's refutation (which was 14 consecutive runs on ONE aged mount -- that measures run-to-run noise at a fixed dose, not a dose-response). Build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, 32/caw, identical knobs, MONOTONE in mount age: (a) FRESH PREP -> sustained_load PASS 32/32, wall 4s/180s, per_op=106ms. (b) after the 5-test aging batch (crash_consistency dir_reuse_coherency fence_during_write fault_netpartition soak) -> PASS 32/32 but wall 44s/180s, per_op=179ms -- an 11x WALL increase for a 1.7x per-op increase. (c) after the FULL 32-node board -> FAIL 180s/180s TIMEOUT, NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=2 then =4 of 32 on consecutive runs, per_op=198ms. THE DECISIVE RATIO: 20 ops at ~198ms is ~4s of actual operations against a 180s wall, so ~97% of the aged wall is spent OUTSIDE the op loop. The degradation is NOT in per-op service time (which moves only 1.7x) -- it is in the criterion's per-node entry/setup path or in whatever the ranks wait on before it. That is a much narrower target than 'the mount is slower', and it is consistent with sess25's finding that statfs is UNCHANGED (71 vs 73 ms) while a single node becomes a 77x outlier. NOT CAUSED BY THE sess28 FIX: with mxfs.dir_epoch_incarn_gate flipped to 0 on the SAME aged mount and the same build, sustained_load failed WORSE (0/32 NO_TERMINAL_RECORD vs 28/32), so the fix reduces the degradation if anything. CHEAP REPRODUCER (~10 min at 32 nodes, no storm needed): prep 32 caw; run.sh 32 caw sustained_load (expect ~4s); run the full board; run.sh 32 caw sustained_load (expect a 180s timeout).

defects.sess28_SECOND_COMPONENT_ROOT_PROVEN_leak: ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b) for the component that remained after the readdir fix. THE DEMOTER CLAIM OUTLIVES ITS HOLDER. CAPTURE METHOD (the part that made it findable): a node that blows the budget produces NO terminal record, so the aggregate line describes only the healthy majority -- which is how this criterion reported per_op=198ms while nodes were stuck. tests/suite/sustained_load.sh now emits per-op progress to /dev/kmsg AS IT HAPPENS (MXFS_SL SLOW/HB/BEGIN/CREATED/READDIR/REMOVED/SYNCED), and tests/sl_straggler_capture.sh sweeps every node for non-heartbeat D-state stacks DURING the run (post-mortem is useless: run.sh kills the test at its budget and the state is gone; the only D-state left afterwards is the normal bounded disklock heartbeat, which must never be convicted). TRAIL: 30 of 32 nodes reach 'SYNCED elapsed=1638..4760'; test21 and test22 stop at 'SLOW phase=rmdir k=8 ms=801/803' and emit nothing further. Reproduced 3 times, SAME two nodes, SAME op index. LIVE STACKS, 5 samples over ~60 s: always msleep inside mxfs_dlm_reload_inode+0x127, but from DIFFERENT PIDs (210880, 210999, 211113) and DIFFERENT syscalls (83 mkdir, 217 getdents64, 257 openat, 262 newfstatat) and different callers (mxfs_dlm_dir_consumer_refresh->xfs_lookup, mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin->xfs_ilock_data_map_shared->xfs_dir_lookup, mxfs_dlm_dir_modify_reload_prelock->xfs_create->xfs_vn_mkdir). So it is NOT one stuck syscall and NOT a deadlock -- EVERY syscall on that node pays the wait. THE WAIT is the sess22 demote-wait at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:19160: `while (mxfs_reload_demote_wait_ms && waited < ... && mxfs_foreign_demoter(ip)) msleep(1);` -- bounded at 50 ms, then P34J-RELOAD-DEMOTE-BAIL and the reload is abandoned with i_dlm_stale still set, so the next syscall repeats it. THE PROOF: test21 = 300 P34J bails, ALL on ONE inode (8926798) with ONE demoter_pid (208840). test22 = 290 bails, ALL on ONE inode (46675531) with ONE demoter_pid (17409). Healthy nodes test5/test13 = ZERO bails and 49 SUCCESSFUL P198 waits. AND BOTH DEMOTER PIDs NO LONGER EXIST -- /proc/<pid> is gone on both nodes while the claim is still set and still being observed. The claim LEAKED: some exit path in the release/BAST drain returned without MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER. mxfs_foreign_demoter() is then true for the life of the in-core inode, which is exactly the 'a mount that must be remounted to stay in budget' symptom this defect is named for. NOTE A LATENT HAZARD FOUND EN ROUTE: ip->i_dlm_demoter is a bare struct task_struct* held WITHOUT a reference, so once the holder exits it is a dangling pointer. mxfs_foreign_demoter() only compares it (safe), but MXFS_SET_DEMOTER's legacy-clobber A/B path dereferences it ((ip)->i_dlm_demoter->pid) -- a use-after-free, reachable only under mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber=1. NEXT: P34J now prints demoter_comm / demoter_line / demoter_age_ms (build 0.11.246, 303E25202F73654C4F056E2). i_dlm_demoter_line is already stamped at every claim, so ONE reproduction names the exit path that failed to clear it. Then fix that path; a dead-holder reclaim is a safety net, not the root fix.
defects.sess28_LEAKING_SITE_NAMED: THE LEAKING CLAIM SITE IS NAMED, first reproduction on build 0.11.246 (303E25202F73654C4F056E2). P34J now prints demoter_comm/demoter_line/demoter_age_ms, and the two populations separate cleanly across 32 nodes: HEALTHY/TRANSIENT (test8, test20, test25, test30): exactly 1 bail each, demoter_line=16541, demoter_comm=kworker/u1x:x, demoter_age_ms=150-156 -- a live drain on a bast kworker, ~150 ms old, self-clearing. LEAKED (test23, the straggler): 224 bails on ONE inode 48234637, demoter_pid=216131, demoter_comm=mkdir, demoter_line=34955, demoter_age_ms=179907 -- a claim held by a SYSCALL context for the ENTIRE 180 s run. test15 showed 354 bails in the same run. LINE 34955 is MXFS_SET_DEMOTER(ip) in the trans deferred-unlock path (mxfs_trans_defer_inode_unlock, just after `if (!igrab(VFS_I(ip))) { mxfs_pal_free(pending); return false; }`). Its own comment says 'Cleared after bast_process completes in mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks' -- so the claim is set in ONE function and cleared in ANOTHER, with the whole remainder of the transaction in between. That is the widest SET->CLEAR span in the file (34955 -> 35082, 127 lines, and across a function boundary); every other pair is 6-75 lines within one function. If the transaction is aborted/cancelled, or drain_inode_unlocks is not reached for that pending entry, the claim is never cleared and, because it was taken by a syscall thread that then exits, mxfs_foreign_demoter() stays true for the life of the in-core inode. NEXT: audit every path from mxfs_trans_defer_inode_unlock's success return to mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks for exits that skip the drain (trans cancel/abort, error unwinds, shutdown), and make the clear unconditional on that path. A dead-holder reclaim is a SAFETY NET, not the root fix. Note ip->i_dlm_demoter is a bare task_struct* held with NO reference, so it dangles once the holder exits -- any fix must not dereference it (mxfs_foreign_demoter only compares, which is safe; MXFS_SET_DEMOTER's legacy-clobber A/B path derefs it and is a use-after-free under mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber=1).

sess29_fix.nesting: i_dlm_punt_n[2] COUNTS retained acquisitions per slot; a bit cannot express nesting (P130-DEFERBAST-DUP lets one tp defer the same inode twice, so both entries can punt).
sess29_fix.sweep: mxfs_demoter_punt_reclaim_check from the two bast workers and the reload demote-wait, grace 5000ms. sess29_fix.recycle_hardening: force both slots NULL in mxfs_dlm_inode_init; new mxfs_dlm_inode_final_release() immediately before kmem_cache_free so an object never re-enters the slab claimed.

defects.ATTRIBUTED_sess25:
THE REFERENCE IS NOW NAMED. sess23's P202-REFEV ring never produced a capture because it is a fixed 10-entry HISTORY window and by unmount has wrapped many times: a leak is an OLD grab with no matching release, which a history window structurally cannot hold. Replaced with P203-GRABLEVELS, a GRAB-BY-REFCOUNT-LEVEL table -- the grab that took i_count to N is recorded in slot N, so with icount=1 slot 1 IS the outstanding reference. Self-correcting: it never has to observe a release, so untracked VFS iput()s cannot desynchronise it.
Captured on the reproducer:
  P203-GRABLEVELS ino=29360571 icount=1 over=0
    P203-LEVEL[1] xfs_lookup+0x16c        <- THE SURVIVOR
    P203-LEVEL[2] mxfs_dlm_bast_notify+0x6f
    P203-LEVEL[3] site=file1:line26265
    P203-LEVEL[4] site=file1:line26690

defects.sess26_attribution_attempt: RATE: 3 catches in 5 full reproducer cycles at 16/caw on builds 8E827AAB / 90C3AAA8 / C142E323, one node per catch (test10, test6, test1). Consistent signature across all three: DIRECTORY, icount=1, dentries=0, hashed=1, lru_linked=1, sblist_linked=1, dlm_mode=3(PR), dlm_state=1(CACHED), itemp=1, in_ail=0, bast/dwork/bwork all NOT pending, demoter=0, nlink 14-18, stale_src 2 or 8, bastq_src 1/9/14. DISPROVEN INSTRUMENT (do not rebuild): a per-inode grab/release BALANCE, added as P205-REFBAL with fields i_mxfs_tgrabs/i_mxfs_tputs. First cut counted only the tracked igrab/iput wrappers and read tgrabs=61 tputs=1 net=60 against icount=1, because MXFS releases via xfs_irele() not iput(). Made symmetric by also counting the xfs_irele() chokepoint and the xfs_iget() hand-off: still tgrabs=161 tputs=83 net=78 against icount=1. The residue is VFS-side references (dput->iput, evict, d_splice_alias's own error-path iput) which cannot be hooked from the filesystem, and Linux has no reverse map from a refcount to its holders. The approach is unsound in principle. P205 is retained only for its honest 'UNEXPLAINED (VFS igrab/iput outside both chokepoints)' verdict. ALSO: P203-LEVEL is sound only under LIFO release order (if grab A takes 0->1 and B takes 1->2 and A releases first, the survivor is B's while LEVEL[1] still names A), so its attribution is PLAUSIBLE not PROVEN. P203-GRABSTACK does not exist in the module at all (strings mxfs.ko = 0 hits) although tests/unmount_leak_repro.sh grepped for it -- that harness has been corrected to grep P203-LEVEL/P202/P205. KEY CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE: dentries=0 with icount=1 means no VFS dentry holds it, yet a lookup-obtained reference survives. xfs_lookup itself was verified to release on every internal path, and xfs_vn_lookup hands the ref to d_splice_alias which consumes it on success and error alike. NEXT (targeted, not global): count per inode how many times xfs_lookup returned 0 handing out a reference, and compare against the dentry count at unmount; lookup_handoffs>0 && dentries==0 && icount==1 shows a lookup reference no dentry ever took. Count d_splice_alias outcomes too, since its error path legitimately consumes the ref via iput without creating a dentry.
