The live hypothesis is that a bast arm igrabbed and the work owning that reference neither reached its trailing irele nor is still pending (every capture shows bast/bwork/dwork/timer all not pending, demoter=0). Arm sites are enumerable via i_dlm_bastq_src (21 assignment sites); captures show src 1, 9, 14. AUDITED AND CORRECT: src=1 (~27113, ilock-end) igrab + queue_work with xfs_irele on queue-false. src=9 at 16613 releases via mxfs_dlm_dwork_safe_irele(ip,3) on queue-false, and at 16866 via xfs_irele on queue-false. src=14 at 13867 and 17816 both pair igrab with queue and xfs_irele on queue-false. The shared PR-demote helper (~32320) also pairs correctly. Note mxfs_dlm_dwork_safe_irele REFUSES to release when i_count<1 or I_FREEING/I_CLEAR (printing P124-DWFN-BADREF) -- but P124 measured 0 on the leaking node, so that refusal did not occur. STILL TO AUDIT: the remaining bastq_src sites (2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11,12,13,15,16 at lines 16094, 16784, 17877, 17972, 18081, 18114, 18260, 25929, 26213, 26688, 26759, 27045, 34464) plus the two generic setters at 32327/32407. Also worth checking whether any site sets bastq_src WITHOUT an accompanying igrab, since the captures' bastq_src only records the LAST arm and may not be the leaking one -- the same last-writer weakness as grab_line.
defects.NEW_ANGLE_sess27_GPT: RULE-5 GPT consult. The load-bearing fact is NOT nlink/PR/CACHED but that the inode is ON THE INODE LRU and later has i_count==1. An inode joins the LRU after becoming unused, so the surviving reference belongs to a NEW BUSY TENURE that began AFTER the inode previously reached zero. That collapses the search to the FINAL 0->1 transition after the last LRU insertion, and needs neither a global lifetime balance nor LIFO pairing -- the two instruments already disproven here. Instrument via a TEMPORARY KERNEL PATCH (ihold() is inline, so module-side instrumentation cannot see it): inode_add_lru(), LRU removal/isolation, __iget(), igrab(), ihold(), iput(), and any direct atomic_long_*(&inode->i_count). Record inode addr/ino/gen, old+new i_count, ts, cpu, pid/comm, stack id, per-inode busy-tenure seq; ring buffer + stack depot, not printk. A kprobe/fentry on generic iput() DOES observe the VFS-side releases (dput->iput, d_splice_alias's internal iput) that are unhookable from the filesystem. A raw ihold()/direct increment from zero is the suspicious case; a normal igrab() of a cached zero-ref inode can be legitimate. FIRST: verify the unmount diagnostic itself does not igrab and manufacture the reported count of 1. SECOND TRACK: vmcore/drgn reverse-search of kernel memory for the inode pointer, classifying the containing object -- and given dlm_state=CACHED, inspect the MXFS DLM object and every reverse pointer from it: 'cached lock object keeps an inode pointer but is not considered pending work' is an ownership category distinct from the queue-arm sites already audited.
defects.sess27_final_tenure_instrument_NEGATIVE: BUILT AND MEASURED, RESULT NEGATIVE (build 0.11.236 8A3F18EEAA6BC0B9475F4C1). GPT's LRU premise was VERIFIED against the kernel source: /src/linux/fs/inode.c __inode_lru_list_add() returns early 'if (icount_read(inode))', so LRU membership proves the inode reached zero. xfs_fs_drop_inode() runs from iput_final() at that transition, so mxfs_inode_tenure_reset() (xfs_inode.h, called from pal/linux/xfs_super.c) now bumps i_mxfs_zero_seq and clears i_mxfs_grabst[] there, scoping the grab table to the final tenure. ALSO VERIFIED: the unmount diagnostic does NOT manufacture the count (mxfs_report_leaked_inodes only atomic_read()s i_count, takes no reference), and evict_inodes() (fs/inode.c:919) skips any inode with a nonzero count, so the survivor is a genuine unreleased ref. BUT the narrowing FAILED: reproduced first cycle at 16/caw (test9 ino 8391875) with 'zero_seq=1 tenure_grabs=499 tenure_age_ms=57533'. The inode hit zero exactly ONCE, 57.5s before unmount, then took 499 tracked grabs without returning to zero -- so the 'final tenure' is a huge busy window and the LIFO objection is fully back. tenure_grabs was added precisely so this failure is visible rather than being misread as an answer. Sites named were all REFUTED on inspection: LEVEL[1]/[2] = xfs_lookup+0x170 = xfs_inode.c:1229 (the xfs_iget return; already eliminated in sess26 because d_splice_alias consumes that ref on every path); LEVEL[4] = xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:27181, the ilock-end BAST arm setting bastq_src=1 -- which MATCHED the leaked inode's bastq_src=1 and looked like a hit, but line 27187 does xfs_irele(ip) on the queue_work-false path and pairs correctly. NOTE: 27181 is a DIFFERENT site from the ~27113 one sess26 audited as 'src=1'; there are at least two sites assigning bastq_src=1 (same one-of-two-variants trap sess26 caught with P142) and both are correct. CONCLUSION: every pairing-based instrument has now failed (global balance, refcount-level table, final-tenure scoping). Switch to the OWNERSHIP question per GPT: preserve a vmcore or run drgn against the LIVE kernel while the leak exists, reverse-search memory for the inode pointer, and classify the containing object. unmount_leak_check.sh must be SPLIT to leave that window -- it currently unmounts AND rmmods before reporting. Inspect the MXFS DLM object (dlm_state=CACHED) and the inode log item (itemp=1, in_ail=0) reverse pointers first.
defects.sess27_P206_OWNERS_all_zero: NEW EVIDENCE, build 0.11.237 EF6935F7BE9995D4AAEB942. Since drgn/crash/gdb and debug symbols are ALL ABSENT from the test nodes (checked), GPT's reverse-search track was done from inside the module for the VFS structures that pin an inode invisibly and that nothing had ruled out. New probe P206-OWNERS, printed beside P202 at unmount. Reproduced 2 of 2 cycles at 16/caw; second capture (test?, ino 29360571): 'P206-OWNERS fsnotify=0 flctx=0 iprivate=0 nrpages=0 readcount=0 dentry_count=0 i_state=0x100 i_opflags=0xb'. EVERY VFS OWNER CANDIDATE IS ZERO -- no fsnotify mark connector, no file_lock_context, no i_private, no page cache, no read-only opens, and a true dentry-alias COUNT of 0 (not just the old boolean). i_state=0x100 is I_REFERENCED, set by __inode_lru_list_add on rotate, consistent with lru_linked=1. CONSEQUENCE: nothing reachable FROM the inode holds the reference. The owner must hold a bare struct inode*/xfs_inode* elsewhere -- an MXFS structure, a work/timer payload (all measured not pending), or a leaked local in a path that igrab'd and returned without storing the pointer. That last category is now the leading hypothesis and is NOT addressable by pairing instruments. This capture also shows the signature varies in its DLM fields across reproductions: capture 1 stale_src=2 bastq_src=1 zero_seq=1 tenure_grabs=499; capture 2 stale_src=8 bastq_src=9 zero_seq=9 tenure_grabs=542. So no single arm site is implicated. GRAB= is the ordinary xfs_iget_cache_hit igrab in both (xfs_icache.c ~1768/1809 -- the SAME site, line numbers shifted by this session's edits; do not read the change as two different sites).
defects.sess27_resolver_drives_the_bast_arms: CONNECTION worth keeping: mxfs_dlm_force_peer_flush() (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~30400) is just mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin(ip, PR) + mxfs_dlm_ilock_end(ip, PR) -- and ilock_end is the site at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:27181 that igrabs and queues the BAST work with bastq_src=1. The xfs_lookup type-flip machinery calls force_peer_flush from BOTH the INODE-REUSE-EVICT retry (xfs_inode.c ~1571, up to 4x) and the P95B resolver loop (every 16th round, up to 201 rounds). So the resolver is the GENERATOR of the bast arms seen on leaked inodes, which is why bastq_src keeps pointing there. The arm site itself is correct (line 27187 xfs_irele on the queue_work-false path) and the INODE-REUSE-EVICT retry is correct too (xfs_irele(*ipp); *ipp=NULL; goto retry_iget). Recorded so the next session does not re-derive the call chain, and so 'bastq_src points at the resolver' is not mistaken for a hit.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (sess36, 0.11.307/308). ROOT (kernel-side kprobe ref-trace, per-inode running-count reconstruction with ZERO anomalies, correlated to module prints at ms precision): mxfs_dlm_bast_notify's four dispatch sites returned without xfs_irele on queue_work()==false, leaking this call's iget ref on every collision with an already-pending work (which owns only the first donor's ref). Live capture ino 8391890: EDEADLK-failed EX acquire -> synchronous deferred-BAST honor -> bast_notify iget -> queue collision (P70-BP starts 10us later) -> P76-QW-FALSE site=immediate -> ref stranded; unmount signature icount=1 dentry_count=0 nothing-pending == every historical capture; prior arm-site audits were clean because the arms ARE clean — the leak was the notify dispatch. FIX: xfs_irele on the queue-false branch at all four sites (the ilock-end arm's existing correct pattern); GPT design review passed (ownership model confirmed; keep-and-park rejected). VERIFIED: (a) deterministic branch-coverage via TEST-ONLY mxfs.bast_qfalse_inject — 126 forced collisions through the fixed branch in one storm, zero queue-false leaks; (b) 8 consecutive clean reproducer cycles on fixed builds (pre-fix catch rate ~0.45/cycle across 11 cycles => P(8 clean unchanged) ~0.8%); (c) kprobe traces armed throughout. RESIDUAL SCOPE NOTE: sites none-held-idle/orphan-release/phantom-reconcile carry the code-identical one-line fix but their triggering recovery scenarios did not occur in any capture or cycle; the only site ever observed firing (immediate) is the demonstrated one. The DISTINCT teardown-ordering leak observed once on an infra-aborted cycle (P142-DWORK-STALE pag=NULL last-ref refusal) is split to D-DWORK-TEARDOWN-LASTREF-LEAK.

defects.summary: A dirent naming a REGULAR FILE resolves to a DIRECTORY inode; the type-flip resolver gives up and the name is durably corrupt cluster-wide
defects.evidence: ccloop c7ee71c6 sess22, 32/caw, after a 20-round sf_mkdir_storm on the same mount. `echo "hello from node 5" > .cache_coherency/cross_visibility/node5.txt` left: stat -> type=directory ino=60823425 size=6 nlink=2 mode=755, while its neighbours node4.txt/node6.txt are correct 18-byte regular files. Every one of the 32 nodes reads node5.txt as empty/absent-as-a-file. MXFS's own probes name it exactly: 'P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT ino=60823425 resolved=0 rounds=201 final_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 name=node5.txt' and 'P-EVICT-RESULT ino=60823425 final_mode=040755 final_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 fop_dir=1 tries=5'. dirent_ftype=1 is XFS_DIR3_FT_REG_FILE, final_ftype=2 is XFS_DIR3_FT_DIR.
defects.scale: Cluster-wide census: 165 P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT events across all 32 nodes; 109 resolved, 56 GAVE UP (resolved=0). All 56 unresolved are the same inode and the same name, i.e. the resolver handles most flips but can fail permanently on one -- and when it does, the corruption is durable and agreed on by every node. Also 196 RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP in the same window.
defects.mechanism: The corruption is in whatever EMITTED the dirent: a name produced by rename_visibility's rename carries ftype=REG while the inode it points at is a live directory of the same incarnation. Likely vector is cross-node inode-number REUSE -- the renamed file's inode was freed and re-allocated as a DIRECTORY by a peer while this node's dirent still claims REG (a dangling dirent surviving a peer's free). Note the adjacent probe RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP fires with incore_mode=0100644 vs disk_mode=040755 and KEEPS the in-core regular-file view over the disk's directory -- i.e. another guard is also picking the wrong side. UNROOTED: find the path that lets a REG dirent survive (or be created) against a live DIR inode.
defects.detector: dirent_type_integrity (tests/suite/dirent_type_integrity.sh, P8, coord=barrier) -- counts unresolved flips in the MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW scoped to the current workload; threshold 0. MUST run after dirent_durability (P6), which stamps the marker; with no marker it FAILs rather than judging stale evidence. cache_coherency catches the user-visible symptom.
defects.blocking_fix: Root the dirent side. The lookup resolver cannot fix this -- both of its outcomes are wrong (publish a mismatch, or ESTALE forever). Fixing it requires either (a) preventing a peer's inode free/realloc from leaving our dirent dangling, or (b) making the dirent's ftype reconcilable against the inode's real type with a defined winner.
defects.reproduction: RELIABLE REPRODUCER FOUND (sess22): 16/caw, criterion `cache_coherency`, rename_visibility subtest. With NO injection armed (typeflip_force_unresolved=0), P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL fired 154 times cluster-wide in one run, e.g. 'ino=17315221 incore_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 incore_mode=040755 name=node12_after_1 comm=ls'. cache_coherency FAILS 0/16 with 'rv new exists node12_after_1' and 'rv content node12_after_1(exp=content_12_1 got=)'. This is FAR more prevalent than the single node5.txt instance first captured, and it does NOT need an aged mount -- it needs the rename workload. Supersedes the earlier 'intermittent, needs storm + heavy tests' note.
defects.attempted_and_refuted: sess27: P206-RENAME-FTYPE-STALE / P206-LINK-FTYPE-STALE -- the hypothesis that xfs_vn_rename/xfs_vn_link snapshot the dirent ftype from i_mode BEFORE the ILOCK (which an MXFS reload can change) so the written ftype can be stale. MEASURED 0 on every node while P201 fired 4x: the written ftype always matched the inode's post-lock type. Probes kept; knob mxfs.rename_ftype_revalidate ships default 0.

sess22_fix_attempt.change: v0.11.183 mxfs.typeflip_fail_unresolved (default 1): when xfs_lookup's P95B type-flip resolver exhausts its 200 rounds without matching the dirent's ground-truth ftype, FAIL the lookup with -ESTALE (drop the ref, leave *ipp NULL) instead of falling through and handing the VFS an inode whose type contradicts the dirent. Probe P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL.
sess22_fix_attempt.rationale: The pre-existing comment called the fall-through 'no worse than the old single-shot behavior'. It is worse: publishing the mismatch is exactly how the corruption becomes durable and agreed by all 32 nodes. -ESTALE is the correct 'revalidate and retry' contract and a reported failure beats silent namespace corruption.
sess22_fix_attempt.exercised: YES. v0.11.184 added TEST-ONLY mxfs.typeflip_force_unresolved to make the resolver give up immediately. Armed cluster-wide + storm: P201 fired 208 times, cache_coherency correctly reported the failure (31/32) instead of silently accepting a wrong-type inode, and ZERO durable type mismatches resulted (all 32 cross_visibility entries regular files).
sess22_fix_attempt.NOT_VALIDATED: The CONTROL arm (force_unresolved=1, fail_unresolved=0, i.e. the pre-fix fall-through) also produced ZERO durable mismatches. So the injection reproduces the GIVE-UP but not the CORRUPTION -- it makes the resolver stop early on flips that would have resolved anyway, rather than recreating the genuine reuse race where the in-core inode really is the wrong incarnation. The fix is principled and its path is proven to run, but it is NOT proven to prevent this defect.
sess22_fix_attempt.no_regression: 32/caw on 0.11.183 with the fix on and no injection: cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, rsync_paired, dir_reuse_coherency all PASS 32/32; two further storm+heavy-test aging cycles all PASS.
sess22_fix_attempt.next_step: Reproduce the genuine unresolved flip. The natural occurrence needed a mount aged by a storm PLUS several heavy criteria; a single storm after a fresh prep does not do it. Either age harder, or inject at the reuse site (bind a REG dirent to a live DIR inode) rather than at the resolver.
sess22_fix_attempt.effect_measured: My P201 change does NOT create failures -- it makes pre-existing ones visible. P201 fires only after the resolver has ALREADY given up 201 rounds, so all 154 would previously have been published as wrong-type bindings. Before: stat reports 'directory' (silent). After: stat reports ESTALE (visible). BUT the ESTALE is PERMANENT, not transient -- the in-core inode never converges, so every subsequent lookup fails too. The name is unusable either way; the fix buys visibility, not correctness. It is NOT a fix for this defect.

defects.which_side_is_wrong: REFUTED (sess27) -- the PLATTER INODE is the corrupt side, not the dirent. sess22 read the child's 'disk' mode through the BUFFER CACHE, the same path under suspicion, so both sides agreed and the reasoning was circular. New probe P207-COHERENT-TRUTH reads the platter with a PLAIN BIO at the resolver give-up: coh_mode=040755 coh_gen==incore_gen, i.e. the platter itself held the PRE-FREE DIRECTORY image. A live inode can never carry a generation older than its own free (EVICT-RING-FLAG showed incore_gen=2697616535 -> freed_gen=2697616536), which is what proves the platter stale. CONSEQUENCE: sess22's blocking_fix 'root the dirent side' aimed at the wrong half, which is why typeflip_fail_unresolved could never fix it.
defects.CORRECTION_prevalence: RETRACTED (sess22, self-caught): the counts I reported as prevalence -- '154 P201 at 16/caw' and '338 P201 on a freshly prepped mount' -- came from UNSCOPED `dmesg | grep -c` runs. prep_cluster does NOT clear the kernel ring and dmesg survives a module reload, so those scans swept in hits from earlier runs on earlier builds. Proof: a standalone run on a freshly prepped cluster read 32 hits that were ALL leftovers (same ino 17315221, same name node12_after_1, OLD probe format from before that build was compiled) while the workload in that run produced zero. PROPERLY SCOPED measurement (dirent_durability stamps MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW, then dirent_type_integrity scans only after it), 16/caw: total_flips=80, unresolved=0, failed_estale=0, stale_skips=57. So type flips are COMMON and are normally RESOLVED; the UNRESOLVED case that produces the corruption is RARE and its true frequency is NOT established. What remains solid is the captured instance itself: node5.txt durably a directory on all 32 nodes, with disk_mode=040755 and disk_gen==incore_gen. The defect is real; my frequency claims were not.

ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.root: RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~20198) kept the in-core inode whenever disk_gen <= incore_gen. XFS generations are RANDOM, so on a genuine cross-node inode-number reuse that comparison is a COIN FLIP; when it lost, the node kept a DEAD incarnation and its release drain PUBLISHED that corpse over the peer's live inode. sess96's own comment two lines above already noted the gen test is unreliable but only patched the case where a lookup supplied a dirent ftype -- with expect_ftype==UNKNOWN (reload from a release/BAST path) the broken comparison was the ONLY discriminator.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.byte_exact_capture: 32/caw ino 10485888 name node15.txt: test15 creates dir gen 2697616535; test15 frees it (freed_gen=2697616536); test15 reuses the number for a REGULAR FILE with new random gen 2379993492; test30 logs RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP incore_mode=040755 disk_mode=0100644 incore_gen=2697616535 disk_gen=2379993492 expect_ft=0 -- reads the CORRECT image and rejects it; test30 then P170-CLWR publishes 10485888:40755:..6535 at realns ...79.98, 2.5s AFTER test15 published 10485888:100644:..3492 at realns ...77.48.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.fix: mxfs.typeflip_skip_same_incarn (default 1): the skip requires disk_gen == incore_gen (same incarnation) -- exactly what sess103 already did for the sibling RELOAD-SIZE-DROP-SKIP and what the guard's own documented target case (sess90 stale-cluster clobber) has. 0 = legacy <= as a same-build negative control. New probe P208-TYPEFLIP-REUSE counts the dangerous subset (different incarnation, lower random gen) in BOTH arms with action=keep|adopt.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.paired_AB_one_build: 0.11.234 EF05E2534A9855795A875F8, knob flipped at runtime, fresh mkfs per arm. A(=0): cache_coherency FAIL 1/32 failed=2; dirent_type_integrity FAIL 5/32 unresolved=4; P208=432 action=keep; STALE-SKIP=432; P201=165; P207=165.  B(=1): cache_coherency PASS 32/32 654/654 23s; dirent_type_integrity PASS 32/32 unresolved=0; P208=223 action=adopt; STALE-SKIP=0; P201=0; P207=0.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.causal_link: An earlier control iteration PASSED with P208=0 -- it never entered the state. The failure tracks the EXPOSURE, not the arm label: exposure>0 + keep = corruption, exposure>0 + adopt = clean.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.reproducer: prep -> dirent_durability -> cache_coherency (3 for 3 pre-fix). dirent_durability's 30-round mkdir/rmdir storm is the AGING pass driving cross-node inode-number reuse; cache_coherency then creates regular files onto the reused numbers. Running cache_coherency FIRST (manifest order, fresh mount) does NOT reproduce it -- which is why the board showed 654/654 green for many sessions. Harnesses: tests/typeflip_ab.sh, tests/inode_cluster_clobber_capture.sh.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.still_open_because: RULE 6 needs testing that exercises the cause to pass cleanly. One paired iteration each so far. Accumulating more paired iterations plus a full-board regression pass on the fix before any disposition.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (RULE 6), ccloop c7ee71c6 sess27, build 0.11.234 EF05E2534A9855795A875F8.  (1) CAUSE PROVEN by RULE 4: byte-exact cross-node timeline for ino 10485888/node15.txt, the guard's own kernel line showing test30 reading the CORRECT new image (disk_mode=0100644 disk_gen=2379993492) and rejecting it, and P207-COHERENT-TRUTH proving via a PLAIN BIO that the platter itself carried the pre-free DIR image -- a generation older than that inode's own free, which no correct FS can expose.  (2) The patch targets exactly that comparison and nothing else, mirroring the sess103 same-incarnation gate already applied to the sibling RELOAD-SIZE-DROP-SKIP.  (3) TESTING THAT EXERCISES THE CAUSE PASSES CLEANLY under UNCHANGED acceptance criteria: the sess27 reproducer (prep -> dirent_durability -> cache_coherency) run 4 times on the fix arm, every run exercising the cause (P208 exposure 223/123/282/233, all action=adopt) and every run clean -- cache_coherency 32/32 654/654, dirent_type_integrity 32/32 unresolved=0, and P201=P207=RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP=0 in all four.  Same-build control arm (knob=0) FAILED 2 of 2 whenever exposure was nonzero (P208 432 and 552, action=keep; cache_coherency FAIL 1/32 and 3/32; dirent_type_integrity FAIL 5/32 and 8/32) and PASSED the one iteration where exposure was 0, i.e. the outcome tracks the EXPOSURE rather than the arm label.  (4) NO REGRESSION: full 32/caw board on the fix -- fio_perf, fio_perf_vs_xfs, cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, dlm_fairness, dlm_membership, scaling_curve, dlm_scaling, rsync_paired, crash_consistency, dir_reuse_coherency, fence_during_write, fault_netpartition, soak, dirent_durability, dirent_type_integrity, node_responsive, kernel_health, sustained_load, dlm_lock_correctness all PASS.  No acceptance threshold was widened; two criteria were made STRICTER this session.

defects.LIMIT_ON_THE_CLAIM: What is proven is that THIS defect -- a dirent whose ftype contradicts the inode it names, produced by RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP retaining a dead incarnation and publishing it -- was fixed under the stated verification.  It is NOT a claim that no untested workload can surface a different stale-image publish.  The knob-0 legacy path remains in the tree only as the negative control.

defects.summary: crash_consistency cannot finish inside its budget at 32 nodes
evidence: sess23 @32/caw on 0.11.194 (BDD132E1285CDEB945565F1): crash_consistency FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 at exactly 90s/90s — every node failed to print a terminal RESULT line before the budget expired. The SAME criterion PASSED 16/16 at 16/caw in 32s/90s on the same build, and the reconvergence gate immediately after it reported all 32 nodes back at active_count=32, so the cluster was healthy — this is the test not completing, not a dead cluster.
defects.mechanism: UNROOTED. NO_TERMINAL_RECORD on every node means the workload did not reach its verdict. Either it scales super-linearly with node count (32s at 16 nodes -> >90s at 32) or it blocks on recovery of the deliberately destroyed node.
defects.detector: ./run.sh 32 caw crash_consistency — FAIL with states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD
defects.blocking_fix: Same as D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE. RULE 0: do not widen the 90s budget.
defects.diagnosis_sess24: ATTRIBUTED BY PER-PHASE INSTRUMENTATION (mxfs-CCph stamps, now in the test). It is NOT a hang and NOT a correctness failure: zero checks fail. Per-phase means at 32 nodes: barrier_ready 0.16s, write 50 files oflag=sync 22.67s, write 50 md5 sidecars 19.50s, barrier_written 7.04s, drop_caches+sleep 3.96s, verify 200 cold files 8.69s => SUM OF MEANS 62.5s, which matches the clean 2x-per-doubling series (1n=2 2n=5 4n=8 8n=16 16n=32s) extrapolated to ~64s. But SUM OF MAX is 98.96s, so the slowest node exceeds the 90s budget; every node then blocks at the final barrier and is killed, producing states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 with no failed check. 68% of the wall (42.2s of 62.5s) is creating 100 small files per node (50 data + 50 .md5) into ONE shared directory — the same mechanism as D-DIR-REUSE-COHERENCY-32-FLAKY. MULTIPATH HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: the recorded 32/cawd=65s and 32/cawp=66s passes are from 2026-07-25/26 on OLDER builds, so the device attribution was confounded; and the CAW attempt census measures CAW service time at 1.5% of grant wait with ZERO io errors, so the dm-multipath command path is not the cost.
defects.disposition_sess24: NOT A PACE DEFECT. It was the wedged node. After recovering test27 (D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK) and re-prepping, crash_consistency PASSES 32/32 at 64s of its 90s budget on the SAME build and SAME device (/dev/mapper/mpatha). 64s is exactly the value the clean 2x-per-doubling series predicts (1n=2 2n=5 4n=8 8n=16 16n=32) and it matches 32/cawd=65s and 32/cawp=66s. The earlier per-phase capture is consistent with this in hindsight: it reported only 27-30 of 32 ranks, and the sum-of-MAX that exceeded the budget (99s) was the sick node dragging the tail while sum-of-means was a healthy 62.5s. Reclassified rather than closed: the cause is now attributed to another OPEN defect, so it is resolved only when D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK is fixed and verified.

defects.diagnosis_sess24: RECLASSIFIED FROM CRITICAL COHERENCY TO MAJOR PACE. The failing run's 'checks=51 passed=50 failed=1 with all 32 nodes agreeing on the wrong answer' is NOT a durable coherent wrong result. The node script emits exactly checks = 7*rounds + 2 (1 ready barrier + 4 barriers and 3 ckeq per round + 1 final pace assertion); this is integral for all 25 recorded conditions (1..32 nodes x caw/cawd/cawp/tcp/xfs), so it is the script's arithmetic, not a coincidence. checks=51 => 7 rounds completed and the ONE failed check is the final pace assertion rounds_done>=8. checks=58 (the passing re-run) => 8 rounds. All 32 nodes agree because rank 1 alone coordinates the time box, so every node evaluates the same rounds_done. Rounds completed vs node count for identical 128-file work: 1n=24(capped) 2n=21 4n=21 8n=17 16n=13 32n=8. The 32-node column sits EXACTLY on the floor. NOT namespace corruption; do not chase a leaf-hash hole.

defects.disposition: DISPROVED as an MXFS defect (sess39, 2026-08-01): the intermittent <8-round failures are driven by host-rig storage-path write-latency degradation, established by measurement fully independent of mxfs. EVIDENCE: (1) failure occurs iff runs execute consecutively; first-run-after->=25min-idle passed 5/5 today (8,9,8,8,9 rounds; two idle-recovery cycles reproduced on schedule). (2) During plateau runs, a pure-host 4K O_DSYNC dd probe on clyde's root fs (no mxfs in path) degrades p90 26->95ms max 164->1806ms, and nvme0n1 block-layer write await (below ext4/SCST) grows p50 1.19->4.29ms p90 15->49ms; the mxfs barrier phases that grew (wrbar/presync/rm/lookups) are exactly the flush/write-bound ones, max-of-32-nodes per barrier amplifying the tails. (3) Same-state controls: on-disk CAW table byte-identical before fast and slow runs; guest CPU flat per-second; xs_sleep_logspace=0 and all log/AIL counters flat; steal-growth artifact traced to fail-path dmesg collection. (4) Rig environment: Samsung 990 EVO Plus (consumer TLC, dynamic SLC cache) 93% full hosting the SCST fileio backing store on the host ROOT fs, with ambient user writers (python3 -m myse: 1.19TB/9h; game server) — consistent with SLC-cache/GC exhaustion under 2000-2600 write ops/s test load, recovering over ~25min idle. RESIDUAL MXFS WORK (already OPEN elsewhere): per-turn EX-rotation economics incl. flush amplification (~85 drain flushes/round) tracked by D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE + D-READDIR-PEER-CACHED-DIR-PACE; grace default 40->10 pending board (fresh+g10 = 9 rounds vs 8 at g40). RIG CONSTRAINT RECORDED: dir_reuse pace results are only comparable from a fresh (>=25min idle) storage state; recommend relocating disk.img off the 93%-full root nvme or pausing ambient writers for pace-sensitive boards.

defects.summary: concurrent create into ONE SHARED directory costs ~42x more wall at 32 nodes than the same creates into per-node private directories, which scale flat
evidence:
Measured on the live 32-node cluster, per-create latency, files written into per-node PRIVATE subdirectories of ONE shared parent so the only contended resource is the parent directory inode (tests/create_scale_curve.sh):
  participants   1     2     4     8    16    32
  p50  ms        5     6     7     8    12    11   <- FLAT in N
  mean ms      5.2   9.2  10.8  26.0  71.7 191.8   <- 37x in N
Shared-dir shape is only ~1.3x worse than private-subdir (247.9 vs 191.8 mean at 32), so dirent/leaf serialisation is SECONDARY; the cost is the parent inode lock. Native local-fs reference on the same nodes: 2.6ms mean. Uncontended MXFS is healthy at 5.2ms.
Stall site read off the kernel, not guessed (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh, 1005 blocked /proc/PID/stack samples): 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep under mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> mxfs_dlm_caw_lock -> caw_wait_for_grant; 14.2% read_slot's SCSI READ(16)+FUA; 4.2% ilock.
CAW attempt census per logical grant (tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh, the measurement GPT named as decisive): CAW submissions mean 6.1 max 33; miscompares mean 5.1 max 32; io errors 0; CAW SERVICE TIME 617ms = 1.5% of 42.1s of grant wait; slot poll READs mean 52.6 max 223. So the wait is ~52 poll cycles per grant, NOT transport service time (1.5%) and NOT CAS throughput (~1.2% at 0.65ms per CAW). The contended resource is ONE directory inode with mixed demand: measured slot masks ino=131 req_mode=PR waiters=0xfb4dffff waiters_ex=0x28440804 holders_pr=0x4820000 holders_ex=0 => 28 waiters of which 6 want EX, 3 hold PR, none holds EX.

sess126 ROOT CAUSE PROVEN BY DIRECT WALL ATTRIBUTION (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, fleet-confirmed). NEW TOOL tests/cc_stackprof.sh + tests/mxfs_stackprof.py: 20Hz /proc/PID/task/*/stack sampling, 8 nodes, 30310 ticks/34300 samples of a virgin-fs crash_consistency run. 26.28% of ALL samples are mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait < caw_nudge_wait < caw_wait_for_grant < mxfs_dlm_caw_lock < mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock; 16.59% are open_last_lookups (queued behind it on the local dir i_rwsem); 39.61% do_wait + 13.59% pipe_read are the parent shells on those same children. Device path, CAS contention and AG locks are ABSENT (<2%). So ~100% of workload blocking wall is the CAW INODE grant wait. THE CONTENDED INODE IS THE MOUNT ROOT, ino 128 (stat /mnt/shared) -- NOT the shared test directory (.crash_consistency = ino 29360256 took ONE >5ms grant, 294ms, all run). Every prior session chased the wrong inode. P138-WAIT is ALWAYS-ON (dlm_caw.c:5918, INODE, >5ms, capped 4000/boot) -- instr=1 is UNNECESSARY and perturbs hard (86s run -> >240s). New harness tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|disarm|report. 202 grant waits >5ms cluster-wide: ino 128 mode=3(PR) 202 grants, 713681ms summed, mean 3533ms, ffw_share 100%, caw_svc_ms 0.8% of wall, caw_miss p50=0. P139-TAILCENSUS n=172: bit_lost=0 (NOT queue-position loss), chosen nonzero 3/172, free_defer 2/172, foreign_yt p50=15 in ALL 172, doze250 p50=15 in ALL 172 => 15 x MXFS_CAW_DEFER_POLL_MS(250) = 3750ms. THE PROOF -- P204-YT-DEFER raw, test5, ino=128, 12 consecutive samples spanning 3 seconds: yt=20000 FROZEN, hpr=8209288 (7 PR holders) BIT-IDENTICAL AND FROZEN, hex=0 (nobody holds EX), wex=27da0000 (10 EX waiters), w growing, age_ms 2037->4980 then the 5000ms MXFS_CAW_YIELD_TIMEOUT_MS stale-ticket valve fires and the cycle repeats. Ticket age at defer ino=128 n=1141: p50=2873 p90=4588 max=4994ms. Queue shape: waiters 19.2, waiters_ex 10.5, holders_ex 0.00, holders_pr 6.79. modes: 3=PR, 5=EX. MECHANISM: (1) a node wants EX on the mount root -- on a virgin fs `mkdir -p $MNT/.crash_consistency` races on all 32 nodes, and the dir is never removed, which is why the SECOND run is fast (sess125's empty-dir recipe was a correct observation with the wrong explanation). (2) A yield ticket is armed for that EX waiter. (3) The 7 PR holders DO NOT RELEASE under the EX BAST for 3+ seconds -- stack evidence 'msleep < mxfs_drain_ilock_read < mxfs_dlm_bast_process < mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn': the release path drains local ilock readers while all 32 nodes path-walk the root continuously for their dd/md5sum opens, so new readers arrive faster than the drain retires them (read-side livelock; nothing bars new readers once a BAST is pending). (4) Meanwhile every PR requester -- COMPATIBLE with the existing PR holders, hex=0 -- is forced to defer on the foreign EX ticket (strict writer preference) and dozes 250ms at a time. (5) Nothing progresses until the 5s valve fires. The system runs on its safety valve. sess24 already documented half of this at dlm_caw.c:155-245 (mxfs_caw_pr_batch_nodefer, default 0): 'a PR requester is COMPATIBLE the whole time and defers purely on policy: strict writer preference, unbounded... yt_age is the wrong clock, the release path re-arms yield_set_ms whenever the ticket VALUE changes.' sess126 confirms it on the ROOT inode at 32 nodes and supplies the other half: the EX waiter the ticket guards can never be granted either.

sess127 (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, VIRGIN fs, hostload 12.68 = quiet rig) RE-ROOTED this at the BAST RECEIVE path and REFUTED the sess126 ilock hypothesis. The run FAILED at 90s/90s. NEW INSTRUMENTS: tests/cc_bastcensus.sh (holder side: pairs the always-on P70-BP ENTRY/EXIT=full by realns and prints a STALLED/UNDELIVERED/CHURN discriminator) and a FOCUS section added to tests/mxfs_stackprof.py + cc_stackprof.sh agg (tick occupancy + full signatures for stacks containing mxfs_dlm_bast*/mxfs_drain_ilock_read, i.e. the release side isolated from the requester side). REFUTATIONS: P132-ILOCK-STUCK/-TIMEOUT = 0 on ALL 32 nodes; FOCUS = 1.18% of 30231 ticks over 8 nodes; msleep<mxfs_drain_ilock_read<bast_process = 4 of 724 focus samples (0.55%) -- the ilock drain is NOT the blocker. P36 is also not the cause: 295 P36-MHT-REARM on ino=128 with pr=0 ex=0 pin=0 in 295 of 295 (so the firing predicate is the unprinted i_dlm_acq_inflight>0), strikes max=10 (~80ms/episode) vs the 2500 strikeout. HOLDER CENSUS ino=128: P70-BP ENTRY=332 EXIT=full=158; ENTRY mode PR=137 NL=187(no-op) EX=8; ENTRY->EXIT release wall p50=319ms p90=1670ms p99=3802ms max=5093ms, >=250ms in 53.2%, >=1000ms in 35; held_ms at BAST entry p50=92203ms (the root tenure spans the WHOLE run). Only 145 real PR/EX release pipelines cluster-wide in 90s = ~1.6 handoffs/s for an inode 19 nodes are queued on -- the limiter is handoff RATE, not release cost. THE ROOT, from FOCUS full signatures (724 samples): 35.22% (255) blk_execute_rq<scsi_execute_cmd<mxfs_pal_scsi_read_fua_bdev<mxfs_pal_bdev_read_prio<read_slot<find_slot_skip<mxfs_dlm_caw_held<mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held<mxfs_dlm_bast_notify<v5_bast_cb<bast_recv_fn; +4.14% (30) the same read under mxfs_caw_orphan_forensic; +0.97% (7) under caw_count_resource_slots<mxfs_dlm_caw_self_held_scan. => ~43% of ALL DLM release-side blocked wall is the single-threaded UDP BAST receive thread doing synchronous SCSI slot reads INLINE. bast_recv_fn (dlm_caw.c:10640) is one thread per node and calls ctx->bast_cb() synchronously inside the recvfrom loop; mxfs_dlm_caw_held() (dlm_caw.c:8493) answers 'do I hold this resource?' -- a question about our OWN bit -- via find_slot() -> a shared-LUN read -> node_held_mode(slot, ctx->node_bit), while the node already keeps ctx->held.slots[]/held.count under held.lock in memory (bast_poll_fn iterates exactly that list) and XFS has ip->i_dlm_mode. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: test5 /proc/net/snmp Udp InErrors=8085 RcvbufErrors=8085 -- every UDP error on the node is a receive-buffer OVERFLOW, i.e. BAST hints are being SILENTLY DROPPED -- and the socket is NOT under-buffered (mxfs_pal_udp_open, pal/linux/kern.c:2420-2426, already sets sk_rcvbuf=4MB + SOCK_RCVBUF_LOCK from sess8), so overflowing 4MB means the thread stalls for seconds. This closes the loop on every earlier number: the holders are not refusing to release, THEY HAVE NOT BEEN TOLD -- sess126's hpr mask bit-identical for 3s, age_ms 2037->4980 before the 5000ms stale-ticket valve, mean grant wait 3533ms, and ~1.6 handoffs/s are all consistent with multi-second BAST delivery latency plus outright hint loss. PRECEDENT MISSED: dlm_caw.h:311-322 (sess35 NUDGE v2) states this exact mechanism for the GRANT NUDGE path -- 'v1 grant nudges woke EVERY blocked acquirer on every node; each did a READ(16)+FUA re-check, and at a 32-node single-dir create convoy those ~28 serialized reads at the one SCSI target WERE the measured ~21.6ms per-handoff latency' -- and fixed it with wake_mask so receivers skip the disk read. The BAST path never got the same treatment.

2026-08-04 sess130 — MEASURED ON 0.11.453 (BAST dispatch queue live, fleet-confirmed F20024E38213A9E64DB6718), VIRGIN fs, quiet console. FIRST, A CONFOUND THAT INVALIDATES THE MAGNITUDES OF THE sess126 BASELINE: tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|mark and tests/cc_bastcensus.sh mark ran `dmesg -n 8`, raising console_loglevel to 8 so every mxfs pr_warn is pushed synchronously to each VM's EMULATED isa-serial console (backed by a host log file). run.sh's prep_cluster sets kernel.printk='1 4 1 1' precisely to avoid this; the mark harnesses silently reversed it. `dmesg -n 8` buys NOTHING for harvesting (printk always stores to the ring buffer; console level gates only the console). PROVEN A/B, same build, same virgin-fs recipe, only the console differs: loglevel 8 -> crash_consistency FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 90s/90s NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 at hostload 11.08, with 7061 mxfs lines written to test1's host serial log; loglevel 1 -> PASS 32/32 79s/90s checks 204/204 at hostload 15.72 — the FAIL was at the LOWER host load. Fixed in tree: tests/quiet_console.sh exports $QUIET_CONSOLE which RE-ASSERTS printk='1 4 1 1'; both harnesses source it. sess126's 'ino 128 mean grant wait 3533 ms' was taken with `arm` (instr=1 AND console 8): its DIRECTION held up, its MAGNITUDE must not be quoted as a clean baseline. SECOND, THE PASS-BAR MEASUREMENTS ON THE QUIET RUN. (a) RcvbufErrors delta across the run = 0, dInErrors = 0, over 614803 datagrams, 32/32 nodes — BAR MET. (b) P138-WAIT cluster-wide: 19 grant waits >5 ms in total, summed 2026 ms, max 495 ms. ino 128: 8 grants, 502 ms summed, mean 62.8 ms, ffw_share 15% — versus sess126's 202 grants / 713681 ms / mean 3533 ms / ffw_share 100%. Summed ino-128 grant wall fell 1422x. The stated bar was mean <50 ms; 62.8 ms on n=8 is ABOVE that line, so that bar item is NOT formally met even though every other discriminator is emphatic. (c) NEW HARNESS tests/cc_yieldcensus.sh (P204-YT-DEFER + P139-TAILCENSUS, both unconditional, no instr): THE SAFETY-VALVE PATHOLOGY IS GONE. P204-YT-DEFER n=567 across 32 nodes, ticket age at defer p50=10 p90=69 max=283 ms, and 0 of 567 (0.0%) within 500 ms of the 5000 ms MXFS_CAW_YIELD_TIMEOUT_MS valve — versus sess126's p50=2873 p90=4588 max=4994 pinned against it. P139-TAILCENSUS: NONE cluster-wide — no grant wait anywhere exceeded 800 ms, versus sess126's n=172 with foreign_yt p50=15 and doze250 p50=15 in ALL 172. Yield tickets are now retired by holders RELEASING, not by the valve. (d) BAST release census on ino 128: P70-BP ENTRY=338 EXIT=full=266 across 32/32 nodes (bar was 'far above 145') — BAR MET. (e) Queue conservation closes exactly: submitted=232310 = new 210078 + merged 8317 + rearmed 13915, overflow=0 inline=0; dispatched=220373 = new 210078 + 10295 requeues (13915 rearm SUBMISSIONS collapse into 10295 requeues); coalescing 1.05x, hiwater=1 — merging carries ~5% of the load, so the fix works by DECOUPLING the socket drain from the synchronous shared-LUN read, not by deduplicating hints. THIRD, AND THE REASON THIS ENTRY STAYS OPEN: THE CREATE-PACE CURVE IS IMPROVED BUT NOT FIXED. tests/create_scale_curve.sh 8 caw on 0.11.453, per-create mean ms by participants [1,2,4,8,16,32]: PRIVATE 4.2/10.9/5.9/19.8/35.2/100.3 (was 5.2/9.2/10.8/26.0/71.7/191.8 — still 24x in N, was 37x); SHARED 3.6/10.2/24.1/35.8/80.7/162.5. Against the sess24 arms: shared-32 mean 255->162.5, p95 2400->1518, node wall 2187->1227; private-32 mean 118->100.3, p95 967->302, wall 1370->889. So SHARED-vs-PRIVATE at 32 nodes is now 1.62x, NOT the headline 42x — the shared-dirent term has largely collapsed — but the PRIVATE arm still degrades 24x from 1 to 32 participants. This entry's summary line ('per-node private directories, which scale flat') is FALSE on the current build. The remaining defect is a MOUNT-GLOBAL O(N) term, not a shared-directory term.

defects.summary: mxfs_dlm_bast_process waits on a FOLIO LOCK while holding the inode DLM/ILOCK, deadlocking against writeback which holds that folio lock and waits for the inode lock — a permanent single-node hang
defects.evidence:
CAPTURED LIVE on test27 (32/caw, build C786A05FF756A6C1C6FF797), both sides of the cycle, from /proc/<pid>/stack:

A) pid 662372 kworker/u9:29+mxfs-ino-bast/dm-1  wchan=folio_wait_bit_common
     folio_wait_bit_common <- __folio_lock <- write_cache_pages
     <- iomap_writepages <- xfs_vm_writepages <- do_writepages
     <- filemap_fdatawrite_wbc <- __filemap_fdatawrite_range
     <- filemap_write_and_wait_range
     <- mxfs_dlm_bast_process+0x5d5 <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn+0x13a
   => holds the inode DLM/ILOCK context, BLOCKED ON A FOLIO LOCK.

B) pid 662838 kworker/u12:30+flush-252:1  wchan=mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin
     mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin <- xfs_ilock <- xfs_map_blocks
     <- iomap_writepage_map <- iomap_do_writepage <- write_cache_pages
     <- iomap_writepages <- xfs_vm_writepages <- do_writepages
     <- __writeback_single_inode <- writeback_sb_inodes
     <- __writeback_inodes_wb <- wb_writeback <- wb_do_writeback
   => holds the folio lock (write_cache_pages locks folios before calling
      iomap_writepage_map), BLOCKED ON THE INODE LOCK.

Pile-up behind the cycle: 4+ `sync` processes in D state at
wb_wait_for_completion / sync_inodes_sb, plus kworker inode_switch_wbs.
loadavg 20.02 vs 0.00 on a healthy peer; a single 1-file write took 69ms vs
11ms. mxfs still mounted, no BUG/WARNING, no filesystem shutdown — the node
looks HEALTHY to every liveness check while being permanently unable to
complete a sync.
defects.lock_order_violated: Upstream XFS/iomap writeback order is FOLIO LOCK -> then xfs_ilock (see write_cache_pages -> iomap_writepage_map -> xfs_map_blocks -> xfs_ilock). Therefore any path that already holds the inode lock must NEVER wait on a folio lock. mxfs_dlm_bast_process calls filemap_write_and_wait_range while holding it, which takes folio locks, and inverts the order. This is the same family as the 'ILOCK held across CAW poll' design tension in CLAUDE.md, but a distinct, concretely captured instance.
defects.blast_radius: ONE wedged node fails the entire 32-node board. Barrier criteria need all N ranks, so the aggregate reads `FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32` — indistinguishable from a totally broken filesystem. Observed exactly that for cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, dlm_fairness and dlm_membership, all on a cluster where 31 of 32 nodes were perfectly healthy. The straggler is nameable from the peers' own reasons: 16 nodes reported `sc node27 last counter(exp=node27_seq20 got=node27_seq1)` while 15 blocked at `sc barrier write-done`. dir_reuse_coherency was UNAFFECTED (still 10 rounds in 110s), which is what proves the filesystem itself was not slower.
defects.blocking_fix: mxfs_dlm_bast_process must not perform a folio-lock-taking writeback (filemap_write_and_wait_range / do_writepages) while holding the inode DLM lock. Options, in order of preference: (1) stage the data flush BEFORE acquiring the inode lock for the BAST, then re-validate under the lock; (2) drop the inode lock across the flush and re-acquire + re-check epoch, the shape already used for dp ILOCK in xfs_create (v0.3.148); (3) if neither is possible, the drain must use a non-blocking writeback and retry rather than wait. NOTE architectural invariant 1: the drain pipeline must still complete before any on-disk unlock, so a bounded retry is required, not a skip.
defects.detection_gap: No criterion detects a D-state mxfs kworker. precond_readiness checks mount + readability, both of which a deadlocked node passes. A per-node D-state / sync-liveness precondition is needed so this reports as a NODE FAULT instead of manufacturing 32 correctness reds.
defects.fix_attempt_sess24:
FIX-27 WRITTEN, SHIPPED DEFAULT OFF, NOT VERIFIED (mxfs.fix27_shared_admit).
Hypothesis: FIX-26 admits the writeback submitter only when it requests EX, but xfs_map_blocks() takes xfs_ilock(ip, XFS_ILOCK_SHARED) first (pal/linux/xfs_aops.c:532), so a folio needing no delalloc conversion requests PR, fails the EX-only gate, parks holding the folio, and deadlocks the drain. FIX-27 widens the admit to shared-class requests from writepages context.
WHY IT IS OFF: measured never to engage. P47-FILEBLOCK (now printing g2, in_wb, in_ioend) census over a healthy 32-node cache_coherency + zero_silent_loss run:
   4435  req=3 mode=0 state=3 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
    181  req=3 mode=0 state=0 g2=0 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
     38  req=3 mode=0 state=3 g2=0 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
     13  req=5 mode=0 state=2 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
      4  req=3 mode=3 state=3 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
TOTAL blocks from writeback OR ioend context: ZERO (in_wb=1 or in_ioend=1 = 0). Blockers are ordinary syscalls: stat 3879, cat 488, md5sum 309, rm 13, bash 10 -- all of which MUST keep waiting; admitting them would be wrong. Turning FIX-27 on produced 0 P25 admits across 3613 shared blocks, and both criteria still passed (and ran slightly faster, 22s/18s vs 27s/28s), with 577 P15-REL-ABORT, so no release-churn harm was observed either way.
NOTE the 4435-row detail: g2=3 (mirror granted PR) means the admit's granted-mode precondition WOULD pass; the only refusal for those is in_wb=0/in_ioend=0. So the admit machinery is healthy and correctly scoped -- the deadlock is a rare race in which a writeback submitter IS the blocker, which this workload never produced.
defects.reproduction_status: NOT REPRODUCED. scripts/fix27_wb_shared_exerciser.sh drives the intended collision (writer rewrites REAL extents with conv=notrunc so map_blocks takes SHARED and never converts -- deliberately inverting FIX-26's v4 lesson that conv=notrunc leaves no delalloc; hot bdi flusher; peer reader storm; mxfs.fix27_delay_ms holds the folio-locked task until the inode is mid-drain). After fixing its predicate to break ONLY into BAST/DEMOTING (v1 broke on ANY state change, including BAST->CACHED, giving 6/68 useless collisions), it reaches 200/200 collisions -- and STILL produces 0 P47, 0 P25 and no wedge in BOTH arms. So the harness makes the submitter collide with a drain but never makes the drain block on THAT submitter's folio, which is the missing half of the cycle.
defects.next_step: 1. P47-FILEBLOCK now prints req/mode/state/g2/in_wb/in_ioend. The next natural occurrence therefore NAMES the failing admit precondition instead of requiring inference from two stacks -- in particular it settles whether the wedged submitter requested EX (xfs_convert_blocks is static and likely INLINED into xfs_map_blocks, so the captured stack cannot distinguish them, and if it was EX then FIX-26 was the relevant admit and some other precondition failed) or SHARED (FIX-27's case).\n2. To reproduce deterministically the harness must synchronise on the OTHER half: make the bast drain's filemap_write_and_wait block on a KNOWN folio, then release the submitter holding exactly that folio. That needs a drain-side marker (e.g. record the folio index the drain is waiting on) rather than only a submitter-side delay.\n3. The node-fault pre-assert in run.sh now BLOCKS and names any sync-wedged node, so a recurrence is caught immediately with its D-state stacks instead of being laundered into 32 correctness reds.
defects.disposition: FIXED_AND_VERIFIED
defects.root_cause_sess25: PROVEN. mxfs_dlm_bast_process calls filemap_write_and_wait at TWO sites and they are not equivalent. Site 1 runs while i_dlm_mode is still the granted mode, so mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin's nest-admit fast path (i_dlm_mode >= request) grants a colliding writeback submitter outright and NOTHING EVER PARKS. Site 2 (the S_ISREG durability flush) runs AFTER `ip->i_dlm_mode = MXFS_LOCK_NL` and BEFORE the wire unlock; mode==NL fails every nest-admit, so the submitter parks in the demote-wait STILL HOLDING ITS FOLIO and this flush blocks on it. That is why sess24's exerciser recorded 200/200 'collisions' with 0 P47/0 P25: it broke out on state==BAST|DEMOTING, which is reached at site 1. The parking precondition is mode==NL, not the state. New field i_dlm_drain_site records which flush the drain is in; P47-FILEBLOCK prints it as dsite=.
defects.reproducer: tests/abba_wedge_ab.sh <drainhost> <peerhost> <0|1> [secs] [stall_ms] -- DETERMINISTIC. New test-only knob mxfs.fix28_drain_stall_ms stalls the drain once, mid-batch, inside its site-2 flush after write_cache_pages has fetched a dirty-tagged folio batch and locked its first folio; a submitter arriving during the stall locks a LATER folio of that batch and parks holding it, and the drain then blocks on exactly that folio. writeback_get_folio() locks UNCONDITIONALLY and works off the already-fetched batch, so the submitter clearing the dirty bit is no reprieve. Harness facts, both measured: the peer must READ (a peer WRITE loop gave 2572 P7B-BASTNOTIFY and ZERO site-2 entries -- EX ping-pong keeps the node re-acquiring so the release never gets that far), and it needs N independent files (one file reached site 2 in only 3 of 4 runs). The script exits 3 INCONCLUSIVE when the hazard was not built, rather than scoring an absent hazard as a pass.
defects.paired_ab_sess25: SAME BUILD 0.11.207 (A797C0480729E0D96999C88), 2/caw, no re-prep between arms. EXPOSURE IDENTICAL: P28-DRAINSITE2 21 vs 21, dirty=1 17 vs 16, P28-DRAINHOLD 17 vs 16, P47-FILEBLOCK 10 vs 10. OUTCOME OPPOSITE: arm0 (fix off) SYNC_WEDGED with both legs captured from /proc/<pid>/stack byte-identical to the test27 live capture and 1 P73-WAITSTALL and 0 admits; arm1 (fix on) SYNC_OK, 0 P73-WAITSTALL, 2 P25-IOEND-ADMIT src=writepages.
defects.single_event_causal_proof: Writing 1 to /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/fix27_shared_admit UN-WEDGED an already-deadlocked node (the demote-wait re-evaluates mxfs_ilock_admit_ioend every 3s), producing EXACTLY ONE probe line: P25-IOEND-ADMIT ino=132 state=3 g2=5 req=3 src=writepages -- state=3 DEMOTING, g2=5 mirror still EX, req=3 SHARED, i.e. precisely the case FIX-26's EX-only gate cannot cover and FIX-27 can.
defects.fix: mxfs.fix27_shared_admit default flipped 0 -> 1 (v0.11.207). sess24 shipped it off because it 'never engaged' under a healthy workload -- a correct measurement answering the wrong question: those 4380 blocks are stat/cat/md5sum which MUST keep waiting, and not firing under health is what a rare-cycle deadlock breaker is supposed to look like. Also added wake_up_all(&ip->i_dlm_wait) before the site-2 flush so a submitter that parked earlier (captured at state=4 ACQUIRING g2=0, when the admit had to refuse) re-evaluates immediately instead of after up to 3s. That wake ALONE IS NOT THE FIX: arm 0 on the build containing it still wedged with 17 hazards built.
defects.safety: Structural, not merely argued: the admit sets i_dlm_mode=EX when the mirror is EX, and the release pipeline's pre-unlock check treats i_dlm_mode != MXFS_LOCK_NL as `stranded` and SKIPS the wire unlock, so an admitted submitter cannot have the grant released out from under it. The anchored release path is protected by its own gen-anchored unlock returning -ESTALE.

defects.summary: mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn's own trailing xfs_irele cascades into inactivation and parks PERMANENTLY in the demote-wait, despite the demoter exemption that exists to cover exactly this
defects.evidence:
ccloop c7ee71c6 sess25, 32/caw on 0.11.207 (A797C0480729E0D96999C88), THREE nodes at once (test7 test8 test13), byte-identical /proc/<pid>/stack, etime 619-839s and MONOTONICALLY CLIMBING on an otherwise QUIESCED cluster:
  mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin+0xf9c <- xfs_ilock+0x198 <- xfs_attr_inactive+0xcd
  <- xfs_inactive+0x59c <- xfs_inode_mark_reclaimable+0x3b0
  <- xfs_fs_destroy_inode+0xf5 <- destroy_inode <- evict <- iput
  <- xfs_irele+0xa6 <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn+0x1a1
The node's own probe names the state, printed every 30s for the whole wedge:
  P73-WAITSTALL ino=31470439 req=5 mode=3 state=3 ex=0 pr=0 pin=0 bast_pend=0 work_busy=2 relflush=1 comm=kworker/u12:9
req=5 EX (xfs_attr_inactive wants ILOCK_EXCL), mode=3 PR held, state=3 DEMOTING, NO holders, and work_busy=2 = the only running bast work IS this worker.
defects.mechanism:
PROVEN by the demoter claim ring (new this session), replayed off a live 32/caw wedge on test16. The ring reads the culprit off directly, no inference:
  P73-DEMEV[8]  SET   line=15980 pid=59368 cookie=446  <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn claims
  P73-DEMEV[9]  SET   line=16280 pid=56068 cookie=449  <- mxfs_dlm_bast_dwork_fn OVERWRITES it
  P73-DEMEV[10] CLEAR line=16292 pid=56068 cookie=450  <- and unconditionally CLEARS it
  P73-DEMEV[11] WAIT  line=25206 pid=59368 cookie=451  <- 59368 parks; demoter_pid=0
i_dlm_demoter was an unqualified single-slot `task_struct *` shared by every release path. The delayed-work drain stored itself over the work drain's LIVE claim and then cleared the slot to NULL. pid 59368's trailing xfs_irele then cascaded into evict -> xfs_inactive -> xfs_attr_inactive -> xfs_ilock, found the slot NULL instead of itself, lost the 'demoter is exempt (it must re-enter during its own drain)' exemption, and parked in the demote-wait forever waiting on a release only it could drive.
defects.detector: node_responsive (tests/suite/node_responsive.sh) -- but ONLY after the sess25 correction below; the pre-sess25 single-sample form could not tell this from ordinary load.
defects.blast_radius: Same as D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK: one permanently-stuck kworker holds the inode tenure, so peers wait on a grant that is never released, and any barrier criterion reports NO_TERMINAL_RECORD on ALL ranks. THREE nodes were in this state simultaneously while every other criterion at 32/caw passed, i.e. it is invisible to correctness tests.
defects.blocking_fix: Root WHO clears the demoter. P73-WAITSTALL now prints demoter_pid / demoter_comm / demoter_line / demoter_age_ms / me= (sess25), so the next occurrence names the clobberer instead of requiring inference. Then either make the claim un-clobberable for the duration of the drain (it is a single-slot field shared by bast_work_fn, bast_dwork_fn and the orphan reclaim), or make the inactivation cascade not need the exemption at all.
defects.detector_correction_sess25: node_responsive's D-state check WAS a single instantaneous `ps` snapshot, which measures LOAD not a wedge -- and the script manufactures that load itself (all N ranks mkdir+rmdir into ONE shared mount immediately before sampling). Measured: 20 of 32 nodes FAILed with dstate=1 right after a dirent_durability storm, 3 of 32 still did on a quiesced cluster, and a manual re-sample 25s later found ZERO D-state tasks anywhere. Corrected to sample twice and convict only a task STILL in D state BY PID after a 10s dwell, reporting pid:comm:wchan. This is strictly MORE specific, not a lower bar: an unchanged-PID wedge trivially survives a 10s dwell (this one had been stuck 600s+), while healthy concurrent I/O does not. The corrected check found this defect on its FIRST run.
defects.note_not_the_abba_defect: DISTINCT from D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK, which was root-caused, reproduced deterministically and fixed in this same session. That one is drain-blocks-on-folio vs writeback-blocks-on-inode, at drain site 2. This one has no folio in it at all: it is the drain worker's own post-drain reference drop re-entering the inode lock. Both present as 'one node cannot finish, board reads 0/N'.

defects.fix: v0.11.210: the claim is now OWNED and NESTABLE. MXFS_SET_DEMOTER claims via cmpxchg only an unowned slot or re-claims its own (depth++), and NEVER overwrites a foreign live claim; MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER releases only if current is the owner, and only the outermost nesting level clears. cmpxchg rather than i_dlm_lock because the call sites disagree about whether that spinlock is held, so taking it inside the macro would deadlock some callers. The 14 '!=' and 2 '==' exemption comparisons in xfs_mxfs_dlm.c plus the reads in pal/linux/xfs_aops.c were routed through the helper. Also converted xfs_inode.c's raw `i_dlm_demoter = current` / `= NULL` pair (inactivation upgrade path) to the new exported mxfs_dlm_claim_demoter/mxfs_dlm_release_demoter helpers -- it was a third instance of the exact clobber shape, bypassing the macros entirely.

  (b) the wedge reproducer still clean (dirent_durability + node_responsive 32/32);

defects.residual: Two release drains still run concurrently on one inode; the fix makes that survivable, not impossible. contest=0 across every run measured, so two slots suffice for observed workloads -- but a THIRD concurrent drain would be refused a slot and would lose its exemption. contest>0 in the census is the standing alarm for that. Separately measured: the wedge SYMPTOM needs three conditions, not one -- (a) no claim at the trailing irele, (b) i_count==1 so it cascades into inactivation, (c) i_dlm_state != NONE so the demote-wait parks. TEST-ONLY mxfs.bast_irele_unclaim_inject forces (a) and fired 646+ times on 4 nodes without wedging, because every i_count==1 sample had state==NONE. A pre-fix arm therefore cannot be expected to reproduce the wedge on demand in this workload; that is why closure rests on the claim-theft census rather than on symptom reproduction.

defects.summary: A node writes the whole 16KB inode CLUSTER to its home location carrying stale images of slots it has no write tenure for
defects.evidence: Captured 32/caw while rooting D-DIRENT-INODE-TYPE-MISMATCH. test30 held ino 10485888 in PR (P71-HOLD mode=3) and its writeback published P170-CLWR 10485888:40755:..6535 -- the PRE-FREE DIRECTORY image -- at realns 1785413079984065412, 2.5s AFTER test15 published the correct new REG incarnation 10485888:100644:..3492 at realns 1785413077486480010. A plain-bio read (P207-COHERENT-TRUTH) then showed the platter holding the pre-free image, i.e. a generation older than that inode's own free. Every P170-CLWR line shows the write unit is the whole cluster: 21+ ino:mode:gen triples per write.
defects.mechanism: The PHYSICAL WRITE UNIT is the 16KB inode cluster, but the coherency protocol locks at INODE granularity. So a node writing one slot it does own republishes whatever it has cached for every neighbouring slot in the same cluster, including inodes a peer owns and has since modified or reallocated. Per the RULE-5 GPT consult (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess27-GPT-verdict-publication-authority-and-lru-tenure): protection must be at least as coarse as the physical write unit, and a compare-and-write used only to manipulate the DLM record does not fence a subsequent ordinary metadata write. Checking ownership only at dirty/queue time is also insufficient -- already-submitted I/O must be drained before an EX downgrade, since an in-flight write can land after another node's commit.
defects.relationship_to_typeflip_fix: mxfs.typeflip_skip_same_incarn (sess27, RESOLVED D-DIRENT-INODE-TYPE-MISMATCH) removes the mechanism that made this node RETAIN a dead incarnation to publish. It does NOT establish write authority, so the class of defect -- publishing an image the node has no tenure for -- remains. GPT's verdict was explicit: keep the equality fix, but classify this separately and deeper.
defects.detector: BUILT sess29 (0.11.253). Site: pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, the held-non-dir branch of the per-slot masking loop -- the `continue` commented 'held non-dir inode -> write it'. That branch is THE GAP: FREE and NL slots are skipped, and a DIRECTORY slot is never written unless logged this round (P56-CORESIDENT-DIR-SKIP), but a non-dir slot is written unconditionally from whatever the cached cluster buffer holds. Probes: P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER (per slot), P218-CLUSTER-AUTHORITY (per write, carries the denominator), P218-CLUSTER-AUTHORITY-TOTAL via `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/cluster_authority_dump`. Census: tests/cluster_authority_census.sh. Detection only -- no knob, no behaviour change.
defects.blocking_fix: One of: cluster-block exclusive ownership; validated read/merge/write under a block lock; or storage compare-and-write over the actual block plus an expected block version. Plus the ordering rules: dirty only while owning the write tenure, drain in-flight I/O before downgrade, and make every publication carry its incarnation + content epoch so a stale publication FAILS rather than overwrites.
defects.detector_design_sess27: NOT BUILT YET -- design plus the primitives that already exist, so the next session does not re-derive them.  SITE: pal/linux/xfs_buf.c ~8223, the P170-CLWR block, which already walks every dinode slot of the cluster buffer being submitted (b_ops == &xfs_inode_buf_ops).  PRIMITIVES: (1) mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held_nb(dlm, ino) is a NON-BLOCKING held-query already used from a context holding pag_ici_lock (see xfs_buf.c ~3349) -- usable per slot here.  (2) struct xfs_buf has b_mxfs_grant_gen (xfs_buf.h:283), 'the owning dir inode's i_dlm_cached_grant_gen at the last COHERENT read of this block; 0 = never stamped', built for exactly this freshness question but currently only for DIR blocks.  (3) P56-CORESIDENT-DIR-SKIP already masks un-logged DIRECTORY slots out of a cluster write ('dir slot not logged this round; skip') -- precedent for the masking approach AND evidence that the general (non-directory) case is unguarded.  THE COUNTING TRAP: do NOT simply count slots the node does not hold EX for.  Roughly 20 of the 21 slots in every cluster write are bytes preserved from whenever the buffer was last read, so that predicate fires on essentially every write and measures nothing.  The meaningful condition is a slot whose bytes could be STALE: the buffer was last read under an OLDER grant than the current one for that slot's inode (the b_mxfs_grant_gen question, generalised from dir blocks to inode clusters), or this node holds an in-core inode for the slot that it has no write tenure for.  Establish the denominator before believing any numerator -- see the sess27 lesson about P208 having to be knob-independent to make an A/B interpretable.

first_measurement_sess29.reading: unlogged_written is the DENOMINATOR and is not itself a defect (ordinary preserved bytes; ~20 of 21 slots qualify on every write -- the sess27 counting trap). no_write_tenure=2970 IS the defect statement verbatim: this node published those slots' bytes while holding them only in PR, i.e. with no write authority. no_incore=68277 is the class P56's directory rationale calls the worst case -- the flushing node holds the cluster cached for a churned child while the slot's own inode is not in core at all, so the bytes are a stale prior-tenure image and no tenure can even be consulted. Writer is xfsaild in every sample.
first_measurement_sess29.honest_limit: The detector measures AUTHORITY, not DIVERGENCE. It proves the node had no write tenure for those bytes; it does NOT prove each one differed from the platter (rewriting identical bytes is harmless). The next step is to pair a nonzero numerator with a plain-bio platter read (the P207-COHERENT-TRUTH primitive) so divergence is measured, not assumed.

defects.sess29_next: 1. Pair the numerator with P207-COHERENT-TRUTH so divergence is measured. 2. no_write_tenure is the smallest and cleanest population (2970) -- start there, not with no_incore. 3. The fix candidates in blocking_fix are unchanged; note that P56's own comment warns an all-skip degenerate case can strand a buffer with no logged inode item, so masking non-dir slots needs that guard too.

divergence_proven_sess29.method: Cross-node timeline merge. P170-CLWR carries every slot of every inode-cluster write as ino:mode:gen-tail:changecount-tail with a CLOCK_REALTIME realns; P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER names the slots a node wrote WITHOUT write tenure. For each passenger, find the last publish of that ino by a DIFFERENT node at least skew_ms earlier and compare. di_changecount is monotone per incarnation, so the merge catches a revert WITHIN an incarnation as well as an incarnation revert -- the first version compared mode+gen only and reported DIVERGENT=0 on 2130 passengers, which was true but blind to the common case.
divergence_proven_sess29.result: 2308 passenger writes, 2306 comparable, 0 blind, DIVERGENT=6. Every one the same shape: a peer published the inode as mode=0 (FREED), and 3.9-4.1 SECONDS later this node published a pre-free mode=100644 image of it with a different generation, from its cached cluster buffer, holding no write tenure. Gap is ~78x the 50ms skew guard, so clock skew cannot manufacture it.
divergence_proven_sess29.why_it_matters: The run that produced this had dir_reuse_coherency PASS 32/32 and dirent_durability PASS 32/32. The corruption is SILENT to the current criteria. This is the same shape sess27 captured by hand (test30 republishing a pre-free DIRECTORY image 2.5s after test15 published the new REG incarnation) -- now reproducible mechanically in a ~3 minute window.
divergence_proven_sess29.instrumentation_hazard: cluster_authority_merge.sh `arm` raises mxfs.instr to uncap probe printing, and that PERTURBS: measured dir_reuse_coherency FAIL 0/32 (111s/120s) with instr=1 vs PASS 32/32 (109s) with instr=0 on the same build. Never run `arm` alongside a criterion verdict. The always-on 800-line/node cap is enough for the merge (32x800 writes) and costs nothing.

defects.severity_note: sess29: divergence is now PROVEN, not inferred. The defect writes a stale pre-free inode image over a slot a peer has already freed, silently, on a passing board.

sess29_fix.knob: mxfs.cluster_passenger_skip — bit0(1)=skip PR-held un-logged slots, bit1(2)=skip un-logged slots with no in-core inode, 3=both (ships 3), 0=pre-fix negative control
sess29_fix.what_it_does: Drops from the inode-cluster write every un-logged slot this node has no write authority for. This is exactly the treatment P56-CORESIDENT-DIR-SKIP already gives an un-logged DIRECTORY slot; the non-dir case was simply never guarded. Per-inode v5 CRCs make writing only the modified inode-sized runs valid. Slots logged or buf-logged this round are NEVER skipped, so a genuine committed change always lands.
sess29_fix.all_skip_guard: P56's own comment warns that an all-skip degenerate case can strand a buffer with no logged inode item. The mask is therefore kept separate and applied only if something survives it; otherwise the pre-fix behaviour is kept for that buffer and counted as `declined`. MEASURED declined=0 across every run.
sess29_fix.ab_same_build: Both arms from a fresh prep, identical workload (dir_reuse_coherency + dirent_durability), window re-marked per arm, knob flipped at runtime. EXPOSURE MATCHED: 2242 vs 2241 passenger slots. control(skip=0): 2242 unauthorised slots WRITTEN, DIVERGENT=3. fix(skip=3): 2241 slots DROPPED, 0 unauthorised slots written, DIVERGENT=0. Both arms passed dir_reuse_coherency 32/32 and dirent_durability 32/32 -- the control's corruption is silent to both criteria.
sess29_fix.no_pace_regression: crash_consistency 65s/90s with the fix on, identical to the pre-fix 0.11.251 baseline (an 85s reading on an aged mount was variance, not the fix). Board at 32/caw otherwise green: cache_coherency 654/654, zero_silent_loss 644/644, dir_reuse_coherency, dirent_durability, fence_during_write, fault_netpartition, soak, node_responsive, kernel_health, dirent_type_integrity all PASS.
sess29_fix.measurement_bug_found_and_fixed: P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER fires while a slot is CONSIDERED, before the mask is applied. Once the fix started dropping slots the merge kept counting dropped ones as publications and reported divergences for writes that never happened. The probe now carries skipped= and the merge excludes them.
sess29_fix.ab_second_node_count: 8/caw, same build, both arms fresh prep, identical workload, window re-marked per arm: control(skip=0) 1446 unauthorised slots WRITTEN, DIVERGENT=10; fix(skip=3) 1482 slots DROPPED, 0 unauthorised slots written, DIVERGENT=0. Both arms passed dir_reuse_coherency 8/8 (114 checks) and dirent_durability 8/8. So the A/B holds at TWO node counts, exposure matched within 2% per pair: 32-node 2242 written/3 divergent -> 0/0; 8-node 1446 written/10 divergent -> 0/0.
sess29_fix.bug_in_the_fix_found_by_gpt_review: nskip counted only the OLD skip rules, so a buffer whose only skips were AUTHORITY skips hit `if (nskip == 0) return false` -- which tells the caller 'not a partial write' and sends the WHOLE buffer, every unauthorised passenger included. The mask was computed and thrown away. The per-slot probe stamped skipped= from the mask at consideration time, so it reported INTENT not OUTCOME and the A/B's '2241 dropped' was an overstatement: after the fix (nskip == 0 && n_pr_skip == 0) the same workload drops 6187, ~2.8x more. Divergence still went 3->0 and 10->0 in the buggy build only because nskip is usually nonzero -- luck, not design. Caught by a design review, NOT by the A/B that passed.
sess29_fix.declined_fallback_replaced: GPT item 1 DONE. The mask is now ALWAYS applied; an empty result is left empty and resolved by obligation state, per GPT's split. empty + nothing owed -> refuse the write outright and complete the buffer with no I/O (P218-WRITE-REFUSED); the no-obligation proof is (logged|bli_dirty)==0, and since `logged` is every inode log item attached to THIS buffer, that PROVES completion cannot satisfy an unsent item. empty + an obligation -> keep the whole write so a committed change is not lost, and shout (P218-SKIP-DECLINED). Measured over a 32-node board: skipped=158218, refused=0, declined=1 occurrence.

defects.why_still_open: Verified at 8/caw and 32/caw. Held OPEN pending the two honest limits stated below, not for lack of node-count coverage. (1) The merge can only judge a passenger that has a prior PEER publish of the same inode inside the max-gap window -- 2 of 2242 at 32 nodes and 2 of 1446 at 8 nodes had none, so a small unjudgeable remainder exists in every run. (2) The fix establishes safety by NOT WRITING bytes it does not own, rather than by acquiring authority over the physical write unit. That is exactly what the pre-existing directory skip already does, and no lost write has been observed (logged and buf-logged slots are never skipped, and `declined` measured 0), but the deeper repair -- write authority at least as coarse as the write unit -- is still the stated blocking_fix and D-RELEASE-BARRIER-OPEN needs it too.
gpt_remaining_work_sess29: 1. REMOVE the `declined` fallback: it reinstates skipped slots when the mask would empty the write -- 'nothing legal to write, so write the illegal bytes'. dirty==0 after the mask implies no logged items and no bli_dirty, so refusing loses nothing, and the helper already owns submission (return true = 'I submitted it').

2. LOGGED SLOTS NEED AN AUTHORITY CHECK. 'Logged this round' proves a JOURNAL representation, not authority to publish to HOME. With D-RELEASE-BARRIER-OPEN: A logs X, releases, B publishes X, A then writes its logged image over B. The DIRECTORY case is already guarded (P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP); non-dir is the same asymmetry one level up.

3. Verify storage-granule alignment / lower-layer RMW safety. Per-inode v5 CRCs detect torn images but do NOT make concurrent sub-block writes safe (512-byte inode writes to a 4Kn device are not independent).

4. Audit EVERY path that publishes an inode-cluster buffer -- log recovery, inode alloc/free, reclaim, unmount flush, error/retry. A recovery path that reconstructs one inode and writes the whole cached cluster reproduces this defect.
5. Split-I/O error handling: one flush becoming several range writes -- decide what stays in the AIL when one range fails.
6. STALE-READ MIRROR: skipped bytes remain in the local cached buffer; a later DLM acquisition must not consume them as authoritative without reload, or a stale-write bug becomes a stale-read bug.
defects.lost_write_safety: STRUCTURAL, not observational: `logged` is built by walking bp->b_li_list -- every inode log item attached to THIS BUFFER -- and a logged or buf-logged slot is never skipped. So a skipped slot provably has no log item for the buffer's iodone to complete; no AIL item is wrongly removed and no dirty state wrongly cleared.

new_finding_sess29_declined.what_it_is: A cluster write where the authority mask empties the write but an obligation exists: ONE logged slot (sector 14) plus 14 unauthorised passengers. dirty==0 means that logged slot is itself inside `skip` -- almost certainly P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP, which deliberately refuses to publish a logged DIRECTORY slot sitting at NL without a RELFLUSH token. So every slot in the buffer is unpublishable, and the pre-existing code whole-writes ALL of them: the dir slot it just decided not to publish AND every unauthorised passenger. This is 'we owe bytes we do not own', exactly the hole GPT named in item 2, seen from the other side.
new_finding_sess29_declined.the_refinement_identified: APPLIED and VALIDATED in 0.11.260. The refusal test is now ((logged|bli_dirty) & ~skip) == 0 -- 'nothing we both OWE and were going to WRITE'. Verified safe by reading the sess19/sess20 chain at P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP: discharging a skipped logged item without its bytes landing is the EXISTING shipped contract for this buffer (i_mxfs_pub_flush_seq is rolled back so the completion's discharge is a no-op, and MXFS_IF_PUB_SKIPPED re-arms it), so refusing adds no new hazard. The old fallback was actively WRONG here: it whole-wrote the very prior-tenure dir slot P56 had just refused to publish, with the ledger already recording that it had not been published. Measured on 32/caw: slots_skipped=71255 writes_refused=18 declined=0 -- the declined branch is now provably unreachable (an owed sector outside `skip` would have to be in `pr_skip`, and pr_skip never takes a logged or buf-logged slot), and it is retained as an assertion. Correctness green: cache_coherency 654/654, dir_reuse_coherency 32/32, dirent_durability 32/32.
new_finding_sess29_declined.rate: 1 occurrence per 32-node board run; loud and always-on, so it cannot regress silently.

sess30_logged_class.gpt_item_2: GPT RULE-5 review item 2: a slot the node DID log this round is still written unconditionally, and 'logged' proves a JOURNAL representation, not authority to publish to HOME.
sess30_logged_class.detector: P219-LOGGED-NO-AUTHORITY (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, at the write path of the logged branch, immediately before its trailing `continue`). Counters via `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/cluster_authority_dump` -> P219-LOGGED-AUTHORITY-TOTAL written/staged/noauth/noauth_dir/stale_tenure/nocore.
sess30_logged_class.primitive: STAGING TENURE STAMP. xfs_iflush stamps i_mxfs_pub_stage_epoch = i_dlm_epoch, i_mxfs_pub_stage_mode, i_mxfs_pub_stage_ns at copy-in (success path only). The cluster-write site compares stage_epoch to the live epoch. i_dlm_epoch is bumped on every grant loss / stale mark, so a mismatch means the tenure that authorized these bytes ENDED before they were published. One 64-bit compare -- no DLM query, no I/O, safe under pag_ici_lock (sess20: the blocking held-query sleeps there).
sess30_logged_class.staged_gate: The comparison is gated on (logged & slotbits), i.e. an inode log item for this slot attached to THIS buffer -- verified: `logged` is built by walking bp->b_li_list. That gate also makes it structurally immune to inode RECYCLING, since a flush-locked inode with an item on a live buffer cannot be reclaimed.
sess30_logged_class.instrument_bug_found_and_fixed: xfs_inode_alloc uses kmem_cache_alloc, NOT zalloc, so a recycled xfs_inode carries any field the mxfs init does not clear. The FIRST measurement read stage_epoch=2 now_epoch=1 on 18 of 22 hits -- an epoch that went DOWN, which a monotonic counter cannot do. Those were recycled inodes whose i_dlm_epoch had been re-initialised to 1 while the stale stamp survived. Fixed by resetting i_mxfs_pub_stage_* in the mxfs inode init. VALIDATE THE INSTRUMENT BEFORE BELIEVING THE NUMERATOR.
