defects.summary: readdir of a directory a peer created costs ~1.2 s per directory; every other syscall on the same inode costs milliseconds
defects.evidence: MEASURED 32/caw, build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh. 32 empty directories in one shared parent, each created by a different node which still holds it cached; then one pass from test1, one syscall class per fresh tree so nothing is confounded: stat 133 ms total (4 ms/op) | open(O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) 1463 ms (45 ms/op) | rmdir 3846 ms (120 ms/op) | opendir+getdents (`ls -f`) 39701 ms (1240 ms/op). Independently reproduced standalone: 32 dirs, readdir-only pass = 37495 ms (1172 ms/op). CONTROL: the identical 32 children created LOCALLY by the same node and removed by it = 152 ms total (4 ms/op) -- so the shared parent is not the bottleneck and neither is the removal. RULE 0: native XFS readdir of an empty directory is microseconds; this is ~10^5x over the ceiling.
defects.mechanism: ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b), build 0.11.245 6764F19681F7272375144DA. xfs/xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1005 -- `for (p48_try = 0; p48_try < 200 && dp->i_dlm_stale && !shutdown; p48_try++) { msleep(1); dp->i_dlm_stale = true; mxfs_dlm_reload_inode(dp, ..., true); }`. 200 x msleep(1) is ~1.2 s at this kernel's timer granularity, which is EXACTLY the observed cost and explains its stability (1201-1215 ms on every sample: the loop always runs its full bound). IT CAN NEVER SUCCEED ON THIS PATH: xfs_readdir holds ILOCK_SHARED across iteration, so the reload's write acquire is blocked by THIS task -- sess14 proved that and made mxfs_dlm_reload_inode bail immediately with P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD. It returns with i_dlm_stale still set, and the loop body re-arms the flag before each attempt, so all 200 rounds bail. P173 was the top probe in the capture (110 lines over 32 dirs = the ratelimited count of 200/dir). The loop's own comment ("ILOCK holds here are sub-ms so waiting is safe") is about OTHER holders; it does not cover the caller being the blocker, which is the case that actually occurs. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS: a phase-split probe on P62 showed mxfs_dlm_reload_inode itself costs tot_ms=0/pre_ms=0/bp_ms=0, so the cost is the sleeping, not the reload. Timed per syscall from python (a real open, not bash's `exec 9<` which returns EISDIR on a directory and made an earlier 45 ms 'open' row meaningless): stat=4ms open=0ms getdents=1202ms close=0ms. REFUTED en route: the pre-readdir wait loop at pal/linux/xfs_file.c:1888 -- its probe P95D-READDIR-WAIT is present in the module (strings) and fired ZERO times.
defects.detector: tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh (~60 s at 32 nodes, no aging needed) -- its phase C prints the four syscall classes side by side and FAILs over a 2x-native ceiling. Also visible as sustained_load's setup phase after tests/suite/sustained_load.sh gained phase timers this session (rmrf=38379 ms of a 38402 ms setup).
defects.blocking_fix: unknown. The shape suggests readdir needs a reload path that can run WITHOUT the caller's ILOCK_SHARED (revalidate before taking the read lock, the way i_mxfs_rd_vgg's 'validate once per grant episode' design intends) rather than one that is structurally guaranteed to bail. Do NOT simply widen the P173 spin: sess14 measured that as a guaranteed livelock for long readers and 350 CPU-seconds per lap.
attempted_and_refuted: FIRST ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG, and the correction is the method lesson. A batch `rm -rf` of the same 32 peer-created dirs measured 38344 ms and I recorded it as ~1.2 s per REMOVAL. Replacing the batch with an explicit per-op rmdir loop over the identical shape gave 993-1052 ms TOTAL (31 ms/op) -- a 37x difference for the same removals. The 1.2 s belongs to the readdir that `rm -rf` performs on each child, not to the unlink. Never attribute a batch wall to the operation the batch is named after; split it per syscall.
Peer-side release latency: REFUTED, drain_ms = 0,0,1 on the creators.
Requester poll quantization: REFUTED by construction, MXFS_CAW_POLL_MAX_MS = 25 ms and the inode fastpoll window is 2 ms for the first 64 ms.
defects.sess28_TIMELINE_NARROWED_TO_PARENT_RELOA: NARROWED FURTHER by an inter-probe delta timeline on the reader (dmesg timestamps, scoped to a fresh marker, 3 children under one shared parent, ~1210 ms per `ls -f` child). THE COST IS NOT ON THE CHILD. Each readdir of a CHILD triggers TWO reloads of the SHARED PARENT (ino 2461, size=36, disk=[n3 n4 n2]), ~600 ms apart, and EVERY ONE IS A NO-OP: 'P62-RELOAD-FORK-SHRINK incore_fmt=1 incore_nx=0 incore_size=36 disk_fmt=1 disk_nx=0 disk_size=36 shrink=0' followed immediately by 'P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL cc=5 gen=1236381809 -- disk == in-core, keeping loaded fork (no destroy/adopt)' and 'P56-RELOAD-MERGE merged=0 clean=1 disk=[n3 n4 n2] ours=[n3 n4 n2]'. Measured gap 48453.955377 -> 48454.561680 = 606 ms between two identical parent reloads that both found nothing. The CHILD's own reload lands 2 ms later. Immediately before each one, P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD fires ~3 times at 3 ms intervals (rd_last=xfs_file_readdir, comm=bash) and bails. THE SUSPECTED LOOP: xfs_dir2_readdir's grant-episode gate (rd_gg != dp->i_mxfs_rd_vgg, xfs_dir2_readdir.c:914) triggers a reload; if the reload BAILS, i_mxfs_rd_vgg is deliberately NOT latched (xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1074) so the trigger re-fires on the next access -- and with 32 peers touching the shared parent, rd_gg keeps moving, so the parent is reloaded again and again, each time discovering it is identical. THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT CLOSES IT: bracket mxfs_dlm_reload_inode with entry/exit timestamps and split the ~600 ms into (a) the coherent grant/verify, (b) the FUA dinode read, (c) the fork rebuild. 600 ms is far too long for a 16 KB FUA read, so the prime suspect is a grant round trip on the hot shared parent -- which would also tie this defect to D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE. Secondary: count reloads per readdir syscall and confirm the no-op repeat is unbounded rather than 2.

defects.summary: CAW yield_to deference starves compatible fresh acquires; retry-budget exhaustion returns -ETIMEDOUT and mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin force-shuts-down the FS — 10 of 32 nodes committed simultaneous voluntary shutdown under dirent_durability
defects.evidence: sess31 (ccloop c7ee71c6), build 0.11.267 srcversion 54BE75FB3219A5A723884FB, QUIET host (load 13/56 cores, NVMe <10%util): run 20260731T042501Z dirent_durability 32/caw FAIL. 10 nodes (test3,5,7,11,20,22,23,25,27,29) each: 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable: ino=139 mode=3(PR) rc=-110 comm=mkdir' within 1.8s (04:28:08.569-04:28:10.337Z). Uniform P-CAWEXH: req=3 our_mode=0 yield_bo=100(or 99) ea_claim=0 ea_compat=0 ea_regwait=0 last_hex=0 last_hpr=0x2088082d. 20/32 nodes logged >=1 full 100-retry exhaustion; every node with 3 consecutive died (P34-ACQ-SLOW attempts=4 dur_ms=7577 rc=-110). Evidence dir: tests/evidence/sess31_dd_shutdown_043430/ (full dmesg all 32 nodes + btime).
defects.mechanism: dlm_caw.c acquire loop: a mode-COMPATIBLE fresh acquire (our_mode=NL) that finds yield_to nonzero and not naming it sleeps and retries (yield_bo path, dlm_caw.c~3392) WITHOUT ever CAS-registering into slot->waiters (registration happens only on the INCOMPATIBLE path ~3619). Releases rebuild the batch ticket as yield_to = cur_slot->waiters (~3971), so the deferrer is invisible to the rotation it defers to; under continuous handoff (~13 rel/s on shared parent ino=139: 32-node mkdir+readdir storm) the ticket never empties and never names it. 100 retries x ~25ms = 2.6s per acquire attempt, x4 ilock_begin attempts = 7.6s, then rc=-ETIMEDOUT which ilock_begin punishes with xfs_force_shutdown (policy: proceeding without grant = uncoordinated metadata corruption). Same rc=-110 signature class as the PREVIOUSLY fixed sess130 (conversion priority) and v0.10.41 (upgrader-yields-to-PR-batch) carve-outs; the fresh-acquire case was never covered.
defects.notes: FIX SHIPPED 0.11.269 (GPT-reviewed option C): (A) mxfs.caw_fresh_register=1 — compatible-yield fresh INODE acquires CAS-register their waiter bit so release tickets (yield_to=waiters) include them; claim CAS clears waiter bits + recomputes waiter_mode atomically (UNCONDITIONAL — also drains pre-existing ghost waiter bits). (B) mxfs.caw_fresh_yield_bound=16 — a registered fresh acquire stops deferring after 16 consecutive yield-only laps and takes the compatible claim (P221-YIELD-BOUND). Verification: pre-fix 3 collapses in 4 same-day sequences; post-fix 5/5 dirent_durability PASS 65-66s, 0 exhaustions (scoped grep P-CAWEXH yreg=), 0 shutdowns, pace unchanged, including at loadavg 22 (worse than the failing era). STILL OPEN: terminal-event paired A/B incomplete — the regime is contention-marginal and did not reproduce post-fix even in control arm (register=0), partly because the unconditional ghost-clear is active in both arms. Complete opportunistically with tests/ysr_dd_ab.sh when the rig next enters the failing regime; tests/yield_starvation_repro.sh is the synthetic (needs barrier-aligned waves to bite). Sess31 note: ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess31-ROOT-FIXED-caw-yield-starvation-shutdown.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (sess36, GPT-ruled). Cause proven sess31 (yield_to deference excluded compatible fresh acquires from release tickets -> 100-retry exhaustion -> ilock_begin forced shutdown; 10-node simultaneous collapse captured). Composite patch 0.11.269 targets the mechanism: fresh-acquire CAS waiter registration, atomic claim-CAS waiter-bit clear + waiter_mode recompute (drains ghost bits), 16-lap yield bound (P221 tracer). Exercised clean since: 5/5 collapse-workload passes at ship, every board green, sess36 +9 aged laps at 2/8 nodes + 32 board with P-CAWEXH=0 on every node; mechanism ENGAGEMENT observed sess36 (P221-YIELD-BOUND fired on test6 — the starvation condition arose, the bound broke it, no exhaustion followed). Paired A/B WAIVED for closure (GPT ruling): the control arm cannot isolate the variable without reverting the foundational claim-CAS change active in both arms — sub-change attribution is optional engineering analysis, not a FIXED AND VERIFIED gate.

defects.summary: crash_consistency cold-read verify: 5/32 observer nodes read IDENTICAL STALE content for two peer-rewritten files (md5 split vs the 27 correct readers) despite sync+drop_caches — a cross-node stale-read coherency failure, cross_write_read family.
defects.evidence: 0.11.292 knob=0 (shipped config), 32/caw, run_id 20260731T131837Z. 5/32 nodes FAILed their durable check: node5_f1 exp=2b88b319... got=38c22ec5... (identical wrong value seen by observers in r2,r3,r4,r5) and node6_f1 exp=175003ea... got=510bde72... (r3,r4,r5,r6). Same got-value across independent observers and rounds = the on-LUN content settled to a stable OLD image, not a torn/flapping read. Extracts: tests/logs/sess33_crash_md5_mismatch/ (all_results.txt, failing_checks.txt, pr_fail_counts.txt); full 3.8G run dir preserved this boot at /tmp/run_crash_consistency_20260731T131837Z (and scratchpad bulk_crash_run). CORRECTED INTERPRETATION (harness read, sess33): crash_consistency KILLS NO NODES (kill coverage lives in the separate real-kill harness); it is write+fsync -> barrier -> drop_caches -> every node cold-verifies every file. 'cc rN' = RANK N (the observer), not a round. So the five FAILing results are observers rank2..rank6 each reading the SAME wrong md5 for node5_f1 (got=38c22ec5) and node6_f1 (got=510bde72) while rank1 and ranks7-32 read the correct fresh values. The test dir persists across laps and files are truncate+rewritten each lap, so got= is almost certainly the PREVIOUS lap's content: a stale extent map / stale cached pages surviving the coherency protocol on exactly those 5 nodes. NOT an on-platter rollback (27 nodes read fresh).
defects.environment_caveats: Host loadavg ~35 during the lap (external game-server burst) — but a wrong md5 is not manufacturable by load; load may have widened the producing race. Multiple nodes logged 'sd 4:0:0:0: PR command failed: 2' during the kill cycles (SCSI persistent-reservation/fence failures under load); test15 also logged P13-SFPARENT-DURABLE-FAIL ino=128 and DLM rc=-35 storms in the window.
mechanism_candidates: 0. COLD-IGET-LAGGING-HOME (now primary): the fs was FRESH this boot — node5_f1 had no prior incarnation, so got= cannot be a previous lap's f1. The 5 observers cold-igot node5_f1's dinode from the LUN while its IN-PLACE image lagged its journal commit (oflag=sync makes data+journal durable, not the home dinode); a lagging dinode = old size/extents = reads of recycled-daddr bytes with a stable wrong checksum. The .md5 companion read fresh on the same nodes (33B file, different path/timing) which is why exp= was correct. The 27 correct readers' PR acquires BASTed the writer and waited out the release drain; the mechanism by which 5 readers bypassed that wait (adjacent ranks 2-6 = a shared window) is the open question — candidates: shared PR grant piggyback where the FIRST reader's drain-wait outcome was consumed pre-landing by the others, or an iget-time read that precedes the DLM acquire entirely.

1. STALE EXTENT MAP: the observers cached node5_f1's inode/extents from the PREVIOUS lap; the truncate+rewrite by node5 moved size/extents; the 5 nodes' revalidation (PR acquire + reload / i_mxfs_rd_vgg-style grant-gen gate for files) did not fire -> they read old blocks. The adjacent-rank clustering (2..6) suggests a shared timing window in the barrier.
2. FUA-READ GATE MISS: reads served from target/page cache without the _XBF_FUA_FRESH platter read where the protocol required one (load-35 widened timing).
3. drop_caches-surviving pages: clean pages pinned/referenced surviving echo-3 while the coherency layer assumed cold. (Would still require the stale-map hazard to matter.)

4. PR-failure lines ('sd 4:0:0:0 PR command failed: 2', multiple nodes, in-window) — crash_consistency does not fence, so these come from lease/heartbeat-adjacent PR activity or residue; treat as environmental until correlated.
5. 291/292 regression unlikely (neither touches read/coherency paths) but a 290 paired lap discriminates cheaply.

defects.summary: A cold-read PR acquire that cannot win the claim-empty CAS within the fixed 100-retry budget returns -110 and mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin escalates it to SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE, cascading the whole cluster
defects.evidence: Repeated at 32/caw on 0.11.334-generation builds during mass cold-read phases (crash_consistency verify after drop_caches; mmap_coherency; zero_silent_loss cross-verify). Signature: 'P-CAWEXH ino=N req=3 our_mode=-1 ea_claim=100 ... last_hex=0 last_hpr=0' then 'P139-LOCKTOTAL rc=-110 retries=100 ea_claim=100 total_ms=1330-1800' then 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable ... shutting down filesystem' + 'Corruption of in-memory data (0x8) at mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:27877)'. Once one node shuts down, its peers' acquires on the same inode time out the same way: 10-32 nodes down per occurrence, board reads NO_TERMINAL_RECORD / pre-assert-not-mounted. ALL retries are ea_claim (claim-empty CAS miscompare), never ea_compat/ea_regwait — so the requester never even registers as a waiter: on-disk census of one stuck resource showed slot LIVE gm=5 hex=1 (one peer holding EX) with waiters=0, i.e. 100 consecutive failures to claim, not a contended grant queue. Timing (~13ms/retry) matches one slot read + one CAW per attempt.
defects.mechanism: UNPROVEN. The claim-empty path retries a fixed MXFS_CAW_MAX_RETRIES=100 times with no liveness extension and no escalating backoff (contrast the WAIT path, which has MXFS_CAW_WAIT_HARDCAP_MS liveness extension, and the UNLOCK path, which has MXFS_CAW_UNLOCK_DEADLINE_MS precisely because giving up there is worse than retrying). Under a 32-way simultaneous cold-read storm every node claims slots for the same inodes at once; each write invalidates the others' compare images. SECOND, INDEPENDENT PROBLEM regardless of the first: a transient CAS-contention timeout is treated as UNRECOVERABLE and escalated to a filesystem shutdown + cluster withdrawal.
ruled_out: Slot-table exhaustion: on-disk census during failures = 556-1845 live of 65536, 63677+ empty.
Pre-mkfs ghost records (different volume id recycled as an insertion point): census shows ONE volume id across all live slots.
Host storage degradation (sess39 rig rule): host fsync probe p50=5.1ms p90=6.5ms taken between failures — healthy band.
sess40 open-tracking work: SAME-BUILD A/B with mxfs.open_tracking=0 (control) reproduces the identical -110 shutdown, so the defect predates increments 3/4 and is not caused by them.
sess40 per-slot iunlink buckets: 0.11.332 (buckets, no open tracking) also showed one crash_consistency 90s FAIL and one 19s PASS — intermittent there too.
defects.detector: P-CAWEXH with ea_claim==MXFS_CAW_MAX_RETRIES, followed by P139-LOCKTOTAL rc=-110 and the ilock_begin shutdown line.
defects.next: THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT NAMES IT: make the claim-exhaustion path print the target empty_idx, the resource's hash base, the slot content AT that index at the last miscompare, and whether a live slot for the resource exists elsewhere (full-probe re-check). That distinguishes (a) genuine 32-way claim contention on one insertion point, (b) a broken probe chain making a resource with a live slot look absent, and (c) a compare-image staleness bug. THEN, independently of the root: the escalation itself is wrong — a claim timeout must not shut the filesystem down; retry with backoff under a wall-clock deadline (the shipped unlock-path pattern), and surface EAGAIN/EIO to the caller rather than SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE.

defects.root_proven_sess40: TRUE ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b) AND IT WAS A SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION FROM 0.11.333, NOT PRE-EXISTING CODE. struct mxfs_caw_lock_slot is an ON-DISK 512-byte sector image. The uint64 open_holders added in 333 was placed after a uint32 field, so the compiler inserted 4 bytes of alignment padding and the struct grew past 512. find_slot's probe reads up to 16 slots at once and indexes that buffer AS AN ARRAY OF THAT STRUCT (span[idx - span_base]), so with an oversized struct every slot past the first in a window decoded from the WRONG BYTE OFFSET. Named outright by the P94-SPAN-DISAGREE byte dump: span16=d4ec3a45acfcd7e69407a00200000000 vs fresh16=4c44584d02000000d4ec3a45acfcd7e6 on the SAME index microseconds apart -- the span image is the true slot SHIFTED BY EXACTLY 8 BYTES (fresh[8..] == span[0..]). CHAIN TO THE SYMPTOM: a shifted image has an unrecognised magic, and slot_appears_corrupt() returns false for any non-LIVE magic so nothing re-read it; find_slot then classified it as 'truly empty', which (1) TERMINATED THE PROBE CHAIN, hiding a live slot that sat further along (explains the on-disk census showing slot LIVE hex!=0 waiters=0 while every requester was in claim-empty), and (2) became the claim's CAS COMPARE image via the last_read_idx==empty_idx skip, so the compare could never match -> claim spins -> retry budget exhausted -> -110 -> mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin escalates to SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE -> 10-32 nodes cascade.
defects.correction_of_my_own_earlier_attribution: The sess40 same-build A/B that appeared to EXONERATE the open-tracking work was INVALID and its conclusion is RETRACTED: mxfs.open_tracking gates BEHAVIOUR, not STRUCT LAYOUT, so both arms carried the broken 520-byte slot. The 'ruled_out' line claiming this defect predates increments 3/4 was therefore wrong. Recorded in full because the reasoning error is the reusable lesson: a knob A/B can only exonerate code the knob actually disables, and a layout/ABI change is never gated by a behaviour knob.
defects.fix: 0.11.341, two parts. (1) LAYOUT: explicit uint32 pad4 before open_holders with reserved[352]; the slot is exactly 512 bytes again and every pre-333 field keeps its original offset. (2) THE MISSING GUARD THAT LET IT SHIP: the size check's kernel arm was a macro, MXFS_BUILD_CHECK_CAW_SLOT(), that NOTHING EVER INVOKED (grep: zero call sites), so kernel builds had NO size assertion at all -- only user-space got the _Static_assert. It is now an unconditional _Static_assert at the point of definition, which needs no call site and fires in every build; the macro remains as a no-op alias. Any future field that breaks the on-disk size now fails the build.

defects.mechanism: MXFS destages cluster buffers eagerly (Mode A coherency) at per-buffer granularity; a crash between the destage of one buffer of a committed transaction and another leaves torn on-disk state that upstream XFS would repair from the log - but MXFS foreign replay treats untagged dead-node images as untrusted and P227 skips the whole transaction, so the log cannot repair the tear either. Any multi-buffer transaction on a dying node has this window; the unlink shape (dirent+inode landed, AGI missed) yields orphans.

defects.summary: Every clean unmount of a PR-protected LUN ends with a FAILED block I/O: the bdev-release cache flush is issued after MXFS has unregistered its SCSI-PR key, so the target rejects it with reservation conflict ('reservation conflict error, dev dm-1, sector 0 op 0x1:(WRITE) flags 0x800 phys_seg 0' + Synchronize Cache(10) FAILED).
evidence: sess43 8/caw on 0.11.353: test8 2 occurrences, test5 1 — each immediately after 'DLM shutdown complete' + xfs_unmountfs (P30-QUIESCE-RECOUNT err=0), i.e. on the bdev-release path

Code ordering (pal/linux/xfs_super.c xfs_fs_put_super): pr_late_key=mxfs_v5_dlm_detach_pr_key (1565) keeps the key across xfs_unmountfs (1580) [v0.11.74 fix]; late unregister at 1583-1590; xfs_shutdown_devices(mp) at 1599 releases the bdev and its flush therefore ALWAYS runs unregistered
Second occurrence shape: the mount-abort path (join refused -> 'MXFS DLM init failed — aborting mount') has the same post-unregister release flush

Rig-wide: bare 'sd N:0:0:0: reservation conflict' notices at every mount are the PR-probe artifact and are NOT this defect; the discriminator is the 'reservation conflict error, dev ...' failed-I/O line

VERIFICATION (tests/unmount_flush_clean.sh, 8/caw on 0.11.354): 24 clean unmount/mount cycles (3 per node x 8 nodes) with ZERO 'reservation conflict error, dev' lines, all 8 nodes remounted. Pre-fix the same path emitted the failed Synchronize Cache on essentially every unmount (measured on 353: test8 x2, test5 x1, and again on test32 during a board unmount). The 50 bare 'sd N:0:0:0: reservation conflict' notices counted in the passing run are the normal PR-probe artifact at mount and are explicitly NOT the defect - the discriminator is the block-layer failed-I/O line.
defects.mechanism: PROVEN by code ordering + timestamps. Durability is not believed to be affected (XFS writes the unmount record and issues its own flush while still registered), but a FAILED I/O on a clean path is not acceptable output and it corrupts every test/health check that greps for reservation conflicts (it produced a false COLLAPSE verdict in tests/vergate_collapse_repro.sh arm c before the detector was tightened).
defects.next_step: Fix candidates: (a) explicit blkdev flush + sync_blockdev BEFORE the late PR unregister so the release path has nothing dirty to flush; (b) hold the PR registration until after xfs_shutdown_devices by taking a bdev reference for the unregister; (c) prove-and-suppress only if (a)/(b) are shown unsafe. Verification: 20 consecutive clean unmounts across >=8 nodes with ZERO 'reservation conflict error, dev' lines.
defects.detector: tests/unmount_flush_clean.sh [N] [cycles] — bar: zero 'reservation conflict error, dev' lines across >=24 clean unmounts
defects.fix: pal/linux/xfs_super.c xfs_fs_put_super: the deferred SCSI-PR unregister now runs AFTER xfs_shutdown_devices(mp) instead of before it. RULE-4 root (proven by code + timestamps, not guessed): xfs_shutdown_devices() ends with an unconditional blkdev_issue_flush() on the data device (inherited upstream, for bdev-pagecache coherency with udev/blkid) and it ran after the unregister, so the target rejected that flush. That function only flushes and invalidates - it does not release the buftargs - so bt_bdev is still valid at the new call site. v0.11.74 had already moved the unregister after xfs_unmountfs (so the unmount log record could not bounce EBADE on a WE-RO target); this completes that ordering so NO device I/O of any kind can outlive our own registration.

(2) A yield ticket is armed for that EX waiter. (3) The 7 PR holders DO NOT RELEASE under the EX BAST for 3+ seconds -- stack evidence 'msleep < mxfs_drain_ilock_read < mxfs_dlm_bast_process < mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn': the release path drains local ilock readers while all 32 nodes path-walk the root continuously for their dd/md5sum opens, so new readers arrive faster than the drain retires them (read-side livelock; nothing bars new readers once a BAST is pending). (4) Meanwhile every PR requester -- COMPATIBLE with the existing PR holders, hex=0 -- is forced to defer on the foreign EX ticket (strict writer preference) and dozes 250ms at a time. defects.opened: 2026-08-03 sess61 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — found by line-reading while implementing GPT's sess57 review item 6B
defects.summary: A peer death detected at ANY point during another node's mount ran the LEGACY IMMEDIATE PURGE instead of the D2 deferred-purge protocol: the dead node's CAW authority manifest was cleared and its heartbeat sector was ZEROED — which is the cluster-wide 'this slice has been replayed' broadcast — for a journal slice nobody had replayed.
defects.found: Code path, line-proven (not a board observation). SHIPPED behaviour in every build from the introduction of the deferred-purge protocol (sess9) through 0.11.405.
evidence: dlm/v5_mount.c:2467-2471 (0.11.405 numbering) — mxfs_v5_dlm_init starts the disklock heartbeat AND wires v5_lease_expire_cb.  This is inside fill_super, BEFORE xfs_mountfs.
pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3080 — mxfs_dlm_cache_init, which registers dead_node_notify_fn (the slice-replay hook), runs AFTER xfs_mountfs(mp) at :3074.

The pre-fix v5_lease_expire_cb gated the D2 deferred path on ctx->dead_node_notify_fn != NULL.  For the whole mount window that hook is NULL, so a detected peer death fell through to the legacy arm: mxfs_dlm_caw_purge_node (clears the CAW authority manifest, which is what the foreign-replay admission gate reads) + mxfs_disklock_purge_node (clears the lock records and ZEROES the dead node's heartbeat sector, dlm/disklock.c:1290-1307).

A zeroed HB sector is the D2 'slice replayed, run your deferred local purge' broadcast: every surviving peer's monitor then fires v5_recovered_cb and releases its deferred purge — for a slice no node ever replayed.

Consequence is exactly the sess9 D2 torn-view defect restored (PROVEN then at drc@16 r13: ifree destaged, dirent-remove abandoned with the log => durable dangling dirent), PLUS destruction of the authority manifest the foreign-replay gate needs, so a later replay of that slice could not be admitted even if one were attempted.

Reachable on the 32-node rig whenever any node reboots or is fenced while another node is mounting.  The mount window is long: log recovery + (when a peer was already frozen) the ~62 s dead-confirm barrier + xfs_log_mount_finish.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: The gate looked like a defensive NULL check on an optional callback.  It was actually a policy decision — 'no replay hook means purge immediately' — applied to the one window in which the hook is guaranteed absent on a node that DOES have a journal and DOES intend to replay.
fix: 0.11.405 (sess61): v5_lease_expire_cb re-gated on dead_slot >= 0 instead of on the hook.  A heartbeat slot means a JOURNAL SLICE, and a journal slice may never be purged before it is replayed regardless of who lacks a hook.  Hook present -> v5_start_slice_recovery; hook absent -> new v5_defer_slice_recovery, which fences, marks recovery pending DURABLY, records slot+node under a new mphase_lock and logs P233-MPHASE-DEATH — purging nothing.  The legacy immediate purge now runs only for a node that owns NO heartbeat slot (pre-claim death, or a peer known only to the TCP/lease layer), which by definition has no slice to replay.
0.11.405: v5_start_slice_recovery split so its elect+notify half (v5_dispatch_slice_recovery) can be deferred.

0.11.406 (sess62): drain API mxfs_v5_dlm_mount_take_late_deaths / _defer_late_deaths; mxfs_dlm_mount_recovery_barrier step (c) restructured into bounded ROUNDS (MXFS_BARRIER_REPLAY_ROUNDS=4) that fold each drain into the next round, so a peer that dies DURING the mount is replayed by this mount rather than left with frozen grants for xfs_log_mount_finish to stall on; mount_cohort_complete stays a SINGLE call after ALL rounds (sess50 cross-slice evidence rule); whatever is not durably replayed is handed back and dispatched by v5_dispatch_late_deaths from mxfs_v5_dlm_mount_settle, which runs after cache_init has registered the hook.
defects.residual: A death detected AFTER the barrier returns still leaves frozen grants that can stall xfs_log_mount_finish up to the CAW wait timeout and then fail the mount; the retry's step 6.5 picks the slot up as a stale cohort member.  Correct but slow.  P233-MPHASE-DEATH names it when it happens.  GPT's item 6A option 3 (mount-time lock acquisition detects and drives recovery of a stale owner) is the only fix that removes the stall, and is unbuilt.
defects.why_still_open: RULE 6: no rig cycle has been spent on this.  The fix is code-proven against the line-proven defect but NOT verified — nothing from 0.11.401 onward has been measured at 32/caw.  Needs a run in which a node is killed during another node's mount, with dmesg showing P233-MPHASE-DEATH (deferral, not purge), the dead node's HB sector still ACTIVE until its slice is replayed, and no peer running a deferred local purge before the replay.

2) Verification run: 32/caw, mount node A while power-cycling node B mid-mount (virsh destroy during A's fill_super).  Assert on A: P233-MPHASE-DEATH slot=<B> and NO mxfs_disklock_purge_node for B before replay.  Assert on a third node C: no v5_recovered_cb for B's slot until after A's foreign replay of it.

defects.opened: 2026-08-03 sess62 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — found while implementing GPT's sess57 review item 6C
defects.summary: Both callers of mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice() DISCARDED its return value, so a dead peer's journal slice whose replay FAILED was published exactly like one that succeeded: CAW authority manifest purged, heartbeat sector zeroed, every surviving peer told the slice was recovered.
defects.found: Code path, line-proven. SHIPPED in every build with live foreign-slice replay (v0.5.0 onward) through 0.11.406.
evidence: xfs/xfs_log.c:797-810 — mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice runs xlog_recover(shadow), calls xlog_recover_cancel on failure, warns 'MXFS: foreign replay of slot %u failed: error %d', and RETURNS that error.

xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42080 (live path, mxfs_dlm_foreign_replay_work_fn) — 'mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice(mp, slot);' with no assignment.  Both surrounding steps (the pre- and post-replay peer_joined_flush) DO check and refuse, so the failure of the replay itself was the only unchecked step in the sequence.
xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42475 (mount barrier step (c)) — same bare call.  The slot then took 'replayed |= (1ULL << slot)' unconditionally and was handed to mxfs_v5_dlm_mount_cohort_complete.

Consequence: the two pieces of durable evidence that would make anyone redo the replay (the CAW manifest and the ACTIVE heartbeat record) are destroyed on the strength of a replay that did not happen.  The dead node's fsync-acked metadata is then unreachable — no later mount and no survivor's re-election sweep has any reason to look at that slice again.

defects.summary: A dead node's journal-slice INTENTS (EFI/EFD, RUI/RUD, CUI/CUD, BUI/BUD) and its AGI unlinked-list obligations are processed by NOBODY, ever, and the slot is nevertheless published as fully recovered and reclaimable. The in-code justification — 'the slice is left dirty so the next mount-time claimer performs full replay including intents' — is FALSE: the next claimer mounts with XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE set, which routes through the SAME xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay() gate and skips the intents again (and skips the images too). The obligation is therefore extinguished with no owner and no durable record that it existed.
defects.found: Code path, line-proven end to end. SHIPPED in every build with per-node log slices + live foreign replay (v0.5.0 onward) through 0.11.407.
evidence: xfs/xfs_log.c:722-740 — mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice()'s own header comment states the premise: 'intent/done items are skipped ... the slice is left dirty, so the next mount-time claimer performs full replay including intents'.

xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:3679-3682 — xlog_do_recover() returns early for FOREIGN_REPLAY right after xlog_do_log_recovery(); xlog_recover_finish() is NEVER reached for a shadow log, so the replayer runs no intents.
xfs/xfs_log.c:797-802 — the shadow xlog's private AIL is kfree()d immediately after xlog_recover() with no drain, so anything pass 2 inserted into it is discarded.

xfs/xfs_log.c:628-632 — a PASS-2 (fresh) disklock claim sets mp->m_mxfs_slice_adopted -> XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE. A slot that has been published-recovered is in EXACTLY that state (its stamp was zeroed by mxfs_disklock_purge_node), so the 'next claimer' is always an adopted-slice mount.
xfs/xfs_log_priv.h:526-531 — xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay() = FOREIGN_REPLAY || ADOPTED_SLICE. Both modes share every skip below.

xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:2224-2244 — under that predicate, XFS_LI_EFI/EFD and XFS_LI_RUI..CUD_RT are 'continue'd with P226-UNTRUSTED-INTENT-SKIP. The comment for the ADOPTED case concedes it 'abandons the dead incarnation's incomplete intents for good — a counted leak'.

xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:2181-2207 — the TRANSACTION-ATOMIC SKIP (default knob mxfs_foreign_replay_untagged_apply=0) taints and drops any transaction containing a BUF/DQUOT/QUOTAOFF/ICREATE item. Essentially every metadata transaction contains a buffer item, so under the default both untrusted modes apply almost nothing at all.

dlm/v5_mount.c:2017-2106 (mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_complete) — publication is CAW purge -> flush -> mxfs_disklock_purge_node (zeroes the dead lock records AND the heartbeat sector) -> clear pending -> beacon. The zeroed HB sector is the cluster-wide 'consumable' broadcast AND the only durable evidence the slice ever needed recovery; ctx->recovery_pending[] is in-memory only.

xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42557-42567 — the mount barrier records the dead slot's AGI unlinked bucket in m_mxfs_sweep_pending_slots for a POST-mount reap worker, then publishes; m_mxfs_sweep_pending_slots is likewise in-memory only, so a crash between publication and the sweep loses the obligation too.

Consequence chain: an abandoned EFI leaves an extent marked allocated in bnobt/cntbt/AGF that nothing references — permanent space leak and a chk_mxfs/repair-visible inconsistency. Abandoned RUI/CUI leave rmap/refcount state that later allocation, unshare and free decisions consume. An abandoned unlinked-list entry leaks an inode with nlink=0 forever.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: Three compounding reasons. (1) The skip is documented as safe by a comment whose premise (the next claimer finishes the job) was never re-checked after sess32 added the ADOPTED_SLICE suppression that invalidated it — the two changes are two years of sessions apart and each is locally reasonable. (2) No criterion exercises it: crash_consistency is guest-side only and fence_during_write leaves no dirty slice, so the board has been green over an entirely unexercised path (the same lesson that produced tests/foreign_replay_ab.sh). (3) The symptom is a leak, not a failure — the FS keeps working, and neither a leaked extent nor a leaked nlink=0 inode surfaces in any current assertion.
fix: NOT YET FIXED. sess63 obtained a RULE-5 design ruling from GPT covering this defect together with GPT sess57 review item 3 (publication staging) and the D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES token campaign's step 4. The binding points of that ruling:

The durable slot state must become a MILESTONE state machine, not a binary ACTIVE/zeroed: ACTIVE -> GUARD{FENCED, IMAGES_REPLAYED, OBLIGATIONS_DONE, GRANTS_RELEASED} -> CONSUMABLE(zeroed). It must carry victim slot + victim incarnation epoch + fs_gen + recovery generation + recovery-owner slot/boot epoch + source slice identity + stage + version/checksum, and must NOT overwrite the victim identity with the recovery holder's.

ORDERING IS FIXED: fence -> CAS ACTIVE->GUARD(FENCED) -> persist -> freeze victim CAW entries -> replay admitted images -> flush -> CAS IMAGES_REPLAYED -> resolve intents+iunlink -> transfer/release grants -> flush -> CAS GRANTS_RELEASED -> zero HB -> beacon. Purging any CAW bit BEFORE the GUARD is durable is a crash hole (HB still reads ACTIVE while half the recovery evidence is destroyed).

The peer broadcast predicate must change. 'Slot no longer ACTIVE' currently means both 'victim fenced' and 'victim grants released'; it must split, or the first GUARD transition tells peers to drop grants that are deliberately still frozen.

A stale GUARD may be claimed as a RECOVERY LEASE but must not become an ACTIVE member slot: the claimant may not set ACTIVE, may not initialise a fresh journal over the victim slice, and may not mount using that slice as its own live log until the obligation reaches CONSUMABLE. This is strictly stronger than the existing sess43 AGI-sweep GUARD semantics.

Intent completion must be done DIRECTLY from the recovery context (option b), not by re-logging foreign intents as ordinary ones (option c): the HB stage byte and the live log are separate durable domains with no atomic commit between them, so a crash between logging the replacement EFI and recording the adoption duplicates the free, and the reverse order loses it. Ordinary xfs_free_extent_later() is NOT sufficient — it gives no deduplicatable {victim slot, victim incarnation, source intent id, adoption generation} identity, and the defer machinery may execute the work during commit/roll rather than leaving a durable pending EFI.

Intent/done matching must use TRANSACTION ADMISSION ON BOTH SIDES: intent admitted + done admitted = cancel; intent admitted + done absent = recover; intent rejected = do not execute, quarantine; intent admitted + done REJECTED = AMBIGUOUS, quarantine, never guess. Honouring a rejected done can suppress required work whose metadata effects were not replayed; ignoring it can double-free metadata that did reach home before the crash. (The rule sess63 proposed — match dones across all transactions, carry forward only admitted intents — was ruled UNSOUND on exactly this case.)

Late completion is safe for EFI only, and only for an atomically admitted intent transaction: the extent is parked allocated-and-unreferenced so no peer can take it. RUI and CUI do NOT inherit the argument (later allocation/unshare/COW/free decisions consume rmap and refcount state) and BUI definitely does not (a peer holding the inode EX can change the range). BUI must be supported correctly or the slice must be quarantined; 'reflink is off in mkfs_mxfs' is NOT a sufficient reason to ignore it.

The AGI unlinked sweep needs more than the allocator argument: nlink==0 does not prove no peer has the inode OPEN. The survivor sweep must hold distributed inode authority integrated with remote-open state, plus AGI/bucket authority; a local iget is not a proof.

Purge-then-reacquire of the victim's AG grants is forbidden. Recovery needs an ATOMIC grant transfer (CAS victim-incarnation-frozen -> recovery-owner/recovery-generation with no unowned interval), a recovery-owner adoption mode, or a cluster metadata freeze.

SEQUENCING: intent recovery is nearly a no-op until the exact-match token gate (campaign step 5) lands, because the blanket ATOMIC-SKIP rejects almost every intent-originating transaction — but shipping step 5 FIRST, with today's early publication, makes things strictly WORSE (many more admitted transactions => many more real pending obligations => still finished by nobody => still published). The durable state machine and the freeze must land BEFORE the gate swap, and step 5 plus intent completion must become active in the SAME compatibility epoch, version-gated so older nodes cannot read a GUARD stage as ordinary non-ACTIVE.
defects.why_still_open: No code has been written. The design is ruled but the protocol (durable milestone descriptor + authority freeze/transfer + intent completion) must be built as ONE unit — GPT's strongest specific ruling is that neither an early CAW purge nor ordinary EFI re-logging without a deduplicated handoff is safe in isolation.

defects.opened: 2026-08-03 sess70 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — proven by reading the PAL preempt call and confirming the target's service-action support on the live rig
defects.summary: The SCSI-PR fence issues PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT / PREEMPT (service action 0x04) instead of PREEMPT AND ABORT (0x05), so the victim's already-in-progress commands are NOT aborted and may land on the shared LUN after the survivor has been told the node is fenced and has begun replaying its journal slice in place
defects.found: Code path, line-proven, plus a live-rig capability probe. SHIPPED in every build since v0.11.80 (D4), which is when fence_node was introduced.
evidence: pal/linux/kern.c:2836-2845 — mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_preempt() calls ops->pr_preempt(dev->bdev, my_key, victim_key, PR_WRITE_EXCLUSIVE_REG_ONLY, false).  The final argument is the kernel block-PR `abort` flag.
/src/linux/include/linux/pr.h:26-27 — the pr_ops prototype is pr_preempt(bdev, old_key, new_key, enum pr_type type, bool abort).

/src/linux/drivers/scsi/sd.c:2204-2209 — sd_pr_preempt() maps the flag directly onto the SPC service action: `sd_pr_out_command(bdev, abort ? 0x05 : 0x04, ...)`.  abort=false is therefore literally PREEMPT, not PREEMPT AND ABORT.

SPC-4 semantics: PREEMPT removes the victim's registration (so every command the target has NOT yet begun processing is rejected with RESERVATION CONFLICT at execution time, because the reservation check happens during command processing) but it does NOT abort the task set of the preempted I_T nexuses.  PREEMPT AND ABORT additionally aborts those tasks and does not complete until they are aborted.  The difference is exactly the in-flight window: with 0x04 a write the victim had already begun executing can still reach the platter after our fence returns 0.

The target on this rig SUPPORTS 0x05 — measured directly, not assumed: `sg_persist --out --preempt-abort --param-rk=<held key> --param-sark=0xdeadbeef1 --prout-type=5 /dev/mapper/mpatha` returned `PR out (Preempt and abort): Reservation conflict`.  RESERVATION CONFLICT is the correct SPC response to preempting an unregistered key and proves the service action was recognised and processed; an unsupported service action would have returned ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID FIELD IN CDB.

The window is not theoretical for the workloads that exercise it: tests/criteria/crash_consistency.sh:69 and tests/criteria/fence_during_write.sh:77 both kill the victim with `virsh destroy` WHILE IT IS MID-WRITE, which is precisely the state in which its task set is non-empty.

Consequence at the call site: dlm/v5_mount.c:715 treats fence_node()==0 as 'fenced', v5_lease_expire_cb (dlm/v5_mount.c:1378) proceeds to v5_start_slice_recovery on the strength of it, and the elected survivor then runs mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice() — in-place XFS journal replay onto the shared LUN — against a node whose outstanding writes were never aborted.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: Three reasons.  (1) The `false` argument is positional and unnamed at the call site, so nothing in the MXFS source spells the word PREEMPT; the distinction is only visible by following the flag into sd.c.  (2) Every comment on this path reasons about FORWARD exclusion ('its next journal write bounces EBADE'), which plain PREEMPT does provide — the in-flight task set is a separate guarantee nobody wrote down.  (3) The rig's own recovery criteria pass, because losing the race requires the victim to have a command mid-execution at the instant of the preempt AND for that command to overlap a block the replay rewrites; both are likely under load but neither is checked by any assertion.

defects.opened: 2026-08-03 sess69 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — found while verifying that the sess68 ruling's required 'completed fence' evidence is producible; ledgered sess70
defects.summary: MXFS_RECOV_STAGE_FENCED is written to the durable recovery descriptor whenever mxfs_scsipr_fence_node() returns 0, but that function returns 0 for four semantically different outcomes — fence completed, victim key already absent, advisory topology (nothing can be fenced), and no PR support at all — so the on-disk record asserts a guarantee that in three of the four cases was never obtained, and no reader can tell which one it was
defects.found: Code path, line-proven end to end.  SHIPPED since 0.11.409, when the durable recovery descriptor went live.  The underlying 'return 0 for advisory' behaviour ships since v0.11.80.
evidence: dlm/scsipr.h:70-78 — the function's own contract: 'Returns 0 when the victim is gone (fenced, never there, or advisory topology)'.  Three outcomes, one return value.

dlm/scsipr.c — the four zero-returns: (a) read_keys returns -EOPNOTSUPP => `return 0` ('No PR support — nothing to fence at the target level'); (b) `count < live_members` => P-PR-ADVISORY log then `return 0`; (c) !own_present && sole survivor => `return 0`; (d) !victim_present => P-PR-FENCE 'already absent' then `return 0`.  Only the path that falls through all four reaches an actual preempt.

dlm/v5_mount.c:686-693 — the call site documents the conflation as deliberate: 'The two zero-returns inside mxfs_scsipr_fence_node that mean "this topology cannot do per-node PR" (P-PR-ADVISORY / -EOPNOTSUPP) still count as fenced here, deliberately ... treating them as failures would make every recovery on a tcm_loop rig unresolvable.'  That is availability being traded for a false correctness claim.

dlm/disklock.c:2234 — `want->recov.desc.stage = MXFS_RECOV_STAGE_FENCED;` is the unconditional consequence: recovery_begin() records the FENCED milestone with no exclusion evidence of any kind passed in, so the descriptor cannot record which guarantee was obtained even in principle.
dlm/disklock.h:296-301 — the stage enum has a single FENCED value and the struct (dlm/disklock.h:319-341) has no field for exclusion kind, fence method, or fence scope.

GPT RULE-5 ruling (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess69-GPT-ruling-advisory-PR-fail-closed-FENCED-is-false), item 4: the outcome must be typed — HARD_PR_DRAINED / PLATFORM_DRAINED / OWNER_QUIESCED_DRAINED / ADVISORY_ONLY / NOT_SUPPORTED / FAILED / STALE_INCARNATION — 'only the first three authorize execution; ADVISORY_ONLY must never advance to an exclusion-proven stage'.  It also requires the two exclusion facts to be kept apart: victim exclusion (V cannot write while its journal is replayed) and previous-recovery-owner exclusion (A cannot continue an old replay after B takes over).  'Do not overload one FENCED stage to mean both.'

Measured on the live rig sess70: this rig is NOT advisory — `P-PR-PROBE 'mxfs': own key visible, N key(s) registered — per-node PR active` on test1/test2/test3, and sg_persist shows one distinct key per node (33 distinct / 64 entries at 32 nodes x 2 multipath paths) with a real `Write Exclusive, registrants only` reservation held.  So the FALSE-claim arm that fires here is (d) 'victim key already absent', which is common: at 32 nodes up to 31 survivors race to fence the same victim and all but the winner take that path.

The descriptor is durable and is read back by the freeze gate (dlm/disklock.c:1393, 1490) and by purge_hb_zeroable(), so the false claim is not merely cosmetic — it is the input to the decision that unfreezes a dead node's grants.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: The conflation was introduced knowingly and documented as safe in a comment whose premise ('D1 EBADE-on-write plus lease/disklock exclusion carry the fencing duty') was never re-derived after the descriptor became a durable, cross-node authority record in 0.11.409.  Reactive D1 fencing cannot help a replay that has already started: it fires on the victim's NEXT write, which is one write too late if the first stale write reaches metadata.  Additionally, no test asserts anything about the descriptor's contents; the criteria only assert that recovery completes.
fix: NOT YET FIXED.  Design is ruled (GPT sess69 item 4, above).  Required shape: mxfs_scsipr_fence_node() returns a typed outcome rather than 0/-errno; the recovery descriptor gains explicit victim_exclusion_kind and owner_exclusion_kind fields with values NONE / HARD_PR_PREEMPT_ABORT / PLATFORM_FENCE_DRAINED / OWNER_CLEAN_QUIESCE / WATCHDOG_RESET_DRAINED / ADVISORY_ONLY; the stage FENCED is renamed to VICTIM_EXCLUSION_PROVEN and may only be recorded when the kind is one that actually proves exclusion.

The wire format is still free to change: no deployed cluster has ever written a descriptor (the format shipped in 0.11.408 and has only ever run on this rig).  Bump MXFS_RECOV_DESC_VERSION rather than reusing bits.
Evidence must be bound to the exact victim incarnation and to the I/O identity/fencing scope, not just the node id — a PR fence of a shared host nexus may fence several nodes or none.
defects.why_still_open: No code written yet.  It is one unit with D-PR-FENCE-PREEMPT-WITHOUT-ABORT (there is no strong kind to record until the fence uses PREEMPT AND ABORT) and with D-VICTIM-REPLAY-WITHOUT-PROVEN-EXCLUSION (recording the kind honestly is pointless unless the replay dispatch actually refuses the weak kinds).

defects.opened: 2026-08-03 sess69 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — GPT RULE-5 ruling; ledgered sess70
defects.summary: A survivor performs in-place XFS journal replay of a dead peer's log slice onto the shared LUN without ever having proven that the peer cannot still write to it — the replay dispatch is gated only on fence_node() returning 0, which as ledgered in D-FENCED-STAGE-WITHOUT-PROVEN-EXCLUSION does not mean the peer was excluded
defects.found: Code path, line-proven end to end.  SHIPPED in every build with live foreign-slice replay (v0.5.0 onward).
evidence: GPT RULE-5 ruling headline (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess69-GPT-ruling-advisory-PR-fail-closed-FENCED-is-false): 'This problem also applies to initially recovering victim V, not only to taking recovery over from A.  If V has not been excluded, replaying V's journal while V can still write is unsafe.'  The defect is therefore NOT confined to the unbuilt takeover coordinator; it is on the shipped live path.

Live path, line by line: dlm/v5_mount.c:1378 v5_lease_expire_cb -> `if (!v5_pr_fence_dead_node(ctx, dead_node)) return;` -> dlm/v5_mount.c:736-739 which is literally `return v5_pr_fence_dead_node_rc(ctx, dead_node) == 0;` -> v5_start_slice_recovery (dlm/v5_mount.c:1294) -> v5_dispatch_slice_recovery -> dead_node_notify_fn -> xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42199 set_bit(dead_slot, m_mxfs_foreign_dead_slots) + queue_work -> xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42090 mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice(mp, slot).  The only exclusion predicate in that chain is the boolean == 0 test.

Mount-barrier path: xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42509 calls mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice(mp, slot) for every slot in the cohort with NO fence predicate in the loop at all — the cohort is computed from stale heartbeat records found at mount time.

Re-election sweep: dlm/v5_mount.c:1272-1288 dispatches replay for OTHER pending slots (p != dead_slot) whose elected replayer just died.  Those victims were fenced (if at all) by a different node at a different time, and nothing re-verifies that the exclusion still holds or ever held.

The replay is in-place and unconditional at the block level: it writes recovered buffer images straight to the shared LUN.  GPT ruled that gating those bulk writes on an authority term is NOT constructible — 'a C&W on the descriptor cannot condition a write to an unrelated LBA' — so there is no downstream check that can catch a stale writer once the replay has begun.

Failure mode: victim V is TCP/heartbeat-dead but disk-alive (partition, long stall, saturated device queue).  Survivor S fences (which, per D-PR-FENCE-PREEMPT-WITHOUT-ABORT, does not abort V's in-flight commands, and per D-FENCED-STAGE-WITHOUT-PROVEN-EXCLUSION may not have excluded V at all), then replays V's slice in place.  V's outstanding metadata writes land on top of, or interleaved with, the recovered images.  Silent metadata corruption, no error reported anywhere.

There is no heartbeat-loss self-fence to bound this from V's side: dlm/disklock.c:534-540 logs `heartbeat write failed` with an age_since_last_ok_ms counter and CONTINUES.  The only self-fence paths in the tree are P131 (device re-mkfs'd under a live mount, dlm/v5_mount.c:1194) and P-PR-SELFFENCE (own PR key found preempted, dlm/v5_mount.c:966-975 and dlm/v5_mount.c:718-723).  A node whose heartbeat has not landed for the full lease keeps mounting, keeps allocating, and keeps writing — which is exactly the state the survivor declares dead and replays.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: The whole design reasons about the fence as a boolean that is either done or not, and every layer above it inherits that framing — v5_pr_fence_dead_node() collapses a four-way outcome to a bool on the very first line.  The criteria that exercise the path (crash_consistency, fence_during_write) kill the victim with `virsh destroy`, which genuinely does exclude it (the qemu process and its iSCSI sessions are torn down by the host), so the tests never present the survivor with a victim that is dead-but-writing.  The dangerous case — heartbeat-dead, disk-alive — is not produced by any test in the suite.
fix: NOT YET FIXED.  Per the GPT ruling the P0 fix is corruption prevention, not design work: block BOTH initial replay and takeover replay when victim exclusion has not been proven, with an explicit, actionable blocked state (e.g. RECOVERY_BLOCKED_NO_IO_EXCLUSION) rather than a silent proceed or a silent stall.

Admissible exclusion evidence per the ruling: PR preempt-and-abort covering that incarnation's distinct I_T nexus with outstanding commands drained; platform/VM/HBA fencing plus I/O drain; an owner-written clean-quiescence ack published only after it stopped submissions and drained; or a rigorously specified watchdog/reset with real timing and drain guarantees.  Liveness conditions (owner not live, descriptor stable for ABANDON_MS) explicitly DO NOT substitute.

'Allowing recovery to proceed would trade an availability failure for possible silent metadata corruption.  For a filesystem, that is the wrong trade.'  The blocked state must come with real escape hatches (hypervisor/BMC/power fencing, SAN port or initiator fencing, full-cluster quiesce plus offline recovery, or administrative submission of a VERIFIED fencing result) — an admin must not be able to simply set a 'fenced' bit.

The heartbeat-loss self-fence is a separate, additive obligation: a node that cannot prove its own heartbeat is landing must stop writing.  Without it there is no software-only construction of the watchdog evidence class at all.
