defects.summary: The CAW slot records lock requests as ONE BIT PER NODE, but a node can have more than one local acquire attempt outstanding for the same resource. The bit therefore cannot say WHICH local request it represents. An attempt that gives up clears `waiters`/`waiters_ex` (and its giveup-mode holder bit) on behalf of the whole node, destroying the on-disk request of a DIFFERENT, still-live local attempt — and the same ambiguity misdirects direct-handoff nomination, which can only name 'node N'.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter() CASes `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit;` plus `holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`, keyed on ctx->node_bit alone — there is no attempt identity anywhere in the slot format or in the call. Three call sites, all post-giveup: grant-wait timeout (dlm_caw.c:3346), claim-exhaustion (4990), convert-exhaustion (6479). Concurrent same-node attempts on ONE resource are possible by design: AG acquires are serialized by pag->pag_dlm_acquire_lock and inode acquires by the MXFS_DLM_ISTATE_ACQUIRING park in mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28138), but the demoter is EXEMPT from that park (!mxfs_is_demoter(ip) at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28141 and 28415) because the BAST drain's trailing xfs_irele must self-reenter. The tree already carries the probe P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28433) labelled in-source as 'the prime suspect for the same-node concurrent-request collision'.
defects.evidence: 32/caw census on 0.11.440 (tests/census_p.sh, 27 of 32 nodes reporting, sess110 board still in the ring buffer): P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ = 0, P6H-ABORT-RECONCILE = 0, 'disk lock acquisition timed out' = 0, P-CAWEXH = 0, P91-CLAIMEXH = 0 on EVERY node, against ~970 P6H-ADOPT per node. So the reconcile arm is never entered under a healthy board and the collision is unobserved — reachable by construction, not by measurement. RULE 6 forbids closing on rarity. GPT (sess111) named this independently as a defect distinct from the holder-adoption race of blocker 6: 'A single waiter bit cannot represent two concurrent local requests, and reg_gen/reg_epoch do not identify which request a handoff satisfies.'
defects.blast_radius: Liveness and correctness. Clearing a live attempt's waiter bit strands that attempt (it polls for a grant that will never be nominated) until its own timeout, and a leaked-or-destroyed waiter bit is the exact shape of the measured 16-node reader-starvation wedge. Clearing a giveup-mode HOLDER bit that a concurrently adopted live tenure depends on is worse: the peer then mints the next epoch and writes while this node still believes it holds the tenure — dual writer.

defects.summary: caw_drop_own_waiter() gives up after 1000 CAS attempts (or on the first hard I/O error, or on a slot read error) and RETURNS NORMALLY. Its callers then return -ETIMEDOUT to the filesystem and the mount continues in normal service with a possibly-leaked waiter or holder bit on the shared LUN. A leaked EX waiter bit has ALREADY caused a measured cluster-wide wedge, so silent exhaustion cannot be treated as successful cleanup.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter(): `for (attempt = 0; attempt < 1000; attempt++)` with backoff capped at 8 ms; `break` on read error, on magic mismatch, on any non-EAGAIN caw_slot() error, and on loop exhaustion. The function is `void` — no caller can tell cleanup succeeded from cleanup abandoned. The in-source comment argues the loop is 'generously bounded so a genuinely wedged slot cannot pin this thread', which trades a thread stall for an unbounded cluster-wide liveness hazard without saying so.
defects.evidence: The sess48 comment block on the same function records the failure this loop exists to prevent: a 16-node barrier-directory wedge where the slot froze at waiter_mode=EX with two orphaned EX waiter bits, every blocked thread across all 16 nodes was a SHARED reader, no thread anywhere was requesting EX, defer_for_waiter starved all readers, cluster phase >600s, posix_semantics_multi16 FAIL. 32/caw census on 0.11.440: the reconcile arm was not entered at all (see D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION), so exhaustion is unobserved.

The direct-handoff adopt arm makes this concrete: it validates the slot image, then calls track_held() — an observe-to-track window in which a concurrent cleanup sees nothing tracked and clears the very holder bit being adopted.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:1982 track_held() records a SLOT INDEX only (no mode), scanning ctx->held.slots[] under ctx->held.lock; dlm_caw.c:2120 untrack_held() removes it. defects.summary: The give-up reconcile clears this node's waiter/holder bits at a REMEMBERED slot index without ever checking that the slot still holds the resource it was remembered for. A slot that was tombstoned and re-claimed for a DIFFERENT resource in the meantime carries our node bit as a live registration for THAT resource — and the reconcile cancels it.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c caw_drop_own_waiter(ctx, slot_idx, giveup_mode) validated only `cur_slot->magic == MXFS_CAW_MAGIC` before CASing `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit; holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`. Live magic is satisfied by ANY live slot, including one now owned by an unrelated resource. Two of the three call sites make this reachable: the grant-wait timeout passes a slot index captured up to a full acquire timeout earlier (MXFS_CAW_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS, liveness-extended), and the claim-exhaustion site passes whatever index the last retry happened to leave in slot_idx — an index the acquire may never have registered on at all. CAW slots are recycled through the tombstone path, so the index is not a stable identity for the resource.
defects.evidence: Line-level: the pre-sess112 function body read the slot, tested magic, and went straight to the bit clears with no memcmp against `resource` — and the function did not even take a resource argument, so the check was not merely omitted, it was unrepresentable. The three call sites are the grant-wait timeout, claim-retry exhaustion and convert exhaustion.
defects.blast_radius: Correctness and liveness on an UNRELATED resource. Clearing a holder bit strips a live local tenure's on-disk write authority (unfenced writer — the same corruption class as D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION, but reaching a resource the abandoning thread never touched). Clearing a waiter bit strands an unrelated acquire until its own timeout. Both are silent: no probe fired on the wrong-resource path because nothing looked.
defects.next: sess112 landed the resource memcmp at the remembered slot on 0.11.441 (the check was previously UNREPRESENTABLE -- the function took no resource argument).  That direction is right but sess113 RULE-5 found the disposition wrong and the debt model structurally broken.  (1) IDENTITY MISMATCH IS NOT DISCHARGE: `if (resource mismatch) { rc = 0; break; }` means 'the remembered location is stale', NOT 'the obligation is complete'.  Recorded debt must survive a mismatch, retarget via a canonical lookup, or escalate.  (2) A SINGLE owed_slot is structurally wrong: several give-ups on one resource can remember DIFFERENT slot indices (the resource moves after a tombstone+reclaim; the claim-exhaustion caller's index is a probe position it may never have registered on), so a later debt silently overwrites an earlier one -- and losing an old waiters_ex clear recreates the measured 16-node wedge.  Model debt as a COLLECTION of exact obligations (resource incarnation, slot index, stable slot-claim cookie, bit classes/modes); note slot->generation is NOT a stable claim identifier because any write bumps it, so this needs a claim epoch that changes only on tombstone/reassign.  (3) A blind re-scan by resource is NOT a safe substitute: ABA on resource reuse, same resource in a NEW slot incarnation, movement during the scan, duplicate claims, and 65536 slots per debt.  (4) A claim-exhaustion probe position the node never registered on should not become HOLDER debt at all. (5) memcmp on struct mxfs_resource_id is only safe if it has no padding and is canonically initialised -- verify, else compare fieldwise.

defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess160 (fix landed 0.11.456 sess157, srcversion 4CA76BE55B7B45177024681; K6 test knob + membership beacon + suite hardening 0.11.457 sess159, srcversion E44F37271ED23D708AFD84C).  CAUSE (found sess156 by code-read, proven on disk sess157): lreq_plan set holder_moot for any give-up mode with e->tenure[mode]!=0 on the mid-run rationale 'its owner's unlock will clear it'.  At teardown that premise is inverted — the owner is departing and will never unlock; the tenure IS the leaked record the drain exists to discharge.  The drain retracted each tenured holder mode with NO CAS, the mask emptied, the retire fired (P263) and memset the tenure record (destroying the evidence), P267 counted completion, and the node claimed a clean departure (no P259) while its holder bit stayed set on the LUN.  0.11.455 thereby leaked the on-disk bit AND suppressed the P248-LREQ-LEAK report 0.11.454 would have made.  sess157 disk baseline: after an injected-CAS-fail departure the owed slot read MXCW-LIVE gen=2 holders_ex=0x1 (departed node_slot 0, granted_mode EX) while in-line-released slots read MXDL-TOMB.  PATCH (design RULE-5-approved sess157): in the frozen teardown world tenured holder modes are NOT mooted — the drain attempts the CAS clear per mode and retires only on confirmed clear or proven absence from the slot image (the PR-tenure moot had been factually harmless only because the PR->EX up-convert CAS had already cleared that bit; the fix CAS-verifies per mode rather than assuming either direction).  Fail-closed tripwires: P269-FROZEN-TENURE-ATTEMPTS (a live local attempt contradicts the frozen premise -> holder clear deferred, obligation stands) and P270-MOOT-RETRACT-REFUSED (a moot verdict reaching a tenured holder in the frozen world is refused, obligation stands).  P271-OWED-DISCHARGE prints every discharged mode — the non-vacuity observable.  VERIFICATION that exercises the cause: (1) deterministic, tests/p248_inject.sh 6/6 PASS on 0.11.457 (sess159, first complete run) with non-vacuity anchors REQUIRED — c1/c4 assert the P271 discharge chain on injected owed departures; c5 (K6 caw_inject_wait_expire forces a contended-acquire give-up, K5 fails the give-up CAS 349us later) proves the obligation STANDS mid-run, no mid-run retire on either node (sess117 guard, p263run=0), then teardown discharges with zero leak; zero P269/P270 across all healthy paths.  (2) ON DISK, tests/p248_disk_proof.sh PASS twice (sess160; second run authoritative after hardening the decoder — od -v to defeat run-length collapse plus strict 16-hex-char validation of all five holder masks, so a decode fault can never pass silently): injected departure (K1=2) on test1, window shows P109 cas_rc=-108 on the owed slot, P257 owed=1 lost=0, P268 n=1, P271 x5 (modes 1-5, tenure=1 on mode 5=EX — the exact tenured-EX case 0.11.455 leaked), P263 tenure=0/0/0/0/0/1, P267 retired=1, NO P259; then a 1MB-granularity scan from the surviving node (the only valid disk-read method — single-sector O_DIRECT through multipath/SCST returns stale data) decoded the owed slot as MXCW-LIVE gen=6 with ALL FIVE holder masks zero of the departed node's bit, while the three in-line-released control slots read MXDL-TOMB (scan-freshness control).  Direct A/B against the sess157 baseline: same procedure, bit present on 0.11.455, bit gone on 0.11.457.  (3) Fleet, tests/p248_census.sh (sess160): 4x './run.sh 32 caw prep_cluster' cycles, three full 32-node teardown windows (two with per-node workload, 8 tracked slots released per node), P248 agg/ENT/KEPT zero, P253/P254/P255/P257/P258/P259/P260/P261/P262/P266/P269/P270/P272 all zero on all 32 nodes in every window, P263/P267/P271 zero (no owed traffic — consistent), 32/32 clean departures per window.
